angle: Cabin additions and the city/county boundary
local: Gatlinburg’s Finance page links overnight-rental procedures and tourist-residency information. Establish whether the parcel is inside the city before using those procedures; a Gatlinburg mailing address is not a substitute for jurisdiction confirmation.
scope: For a cabin with an expanded deck, new hot tub, and access improvements, separate the building project from equipment and site work. Ask for an itemized contractor scope identifying what supports the structure and what serves a separate function. A guest-amenity label does not classify the entire invoice. If the cabin already has a depreciation schedule, reconcile additions to that schedule before commissioning a whole-property estimate.
records: City or county jurisdiction confirmation and the parcel identifier
Deck drawings, hot-tub purchase records, and electrical scope
Original cabin schedule plus dates each later addition became ready for guests
scenario: A buyer acquires an operating cabin and adds a second deck before reopening. Prepare separate cost pools for the acquired property, seller furnishings, and new work. Give the preparer the closing inventory and the contractor’s description of the deck foundation; one total remodeling payment cannot explain all three pools.
question: Does a Sevier County permit file cover my Gatlinburg cabin?
answer: Confirm the actual parcel jurisdiction first. Retain the applicable city or county records as part of the operating file, but use purchase and construction evidence to establish study costs. Permit paperwork and component valuation serve different purposes.

angle: A postal address can cover different permitting authorities
local: The city publishes its own STR application guide. Sevier County separately publishes an application for its unincorporated areas. Determine which authority covers the cabin before building the operating timeline; do not treat the two applications as interchangeable.
scope: A newly completed cabin can have land acquisition, a construction contract, owner-purchased appliances, and furnishings ordered outside the builder’s budget. Create a sources-and-uses reconciliation before the study. Attach approved changes to the original contract and distinguish deposits from final invoices. Ask the provider how it will handle unfinished exterior work instead of treating the first guest booking as the completion date for every asset.
records: Parcel and jurisdiction confirmation, including city-limit status
Builder schedule of values with change orders and payment reconciliation
Owner-furnished equipment invoices and separate completion dates
scenario: A construction draw includes an allowance for appliances, but the owner buys upgraded appliances directly. Compare the builder’s final credit with the owner’s invoices. Without that step, the same allowance can remain in the building budget while the actual appliances are listed again as a separate purchase.
question: Can the builder’s total contract price be the entire study file?
answer: It is a starting point. Owner purchases, allowance credits, site costs, and changes can make the contract total differ from the final capitalized costs. Supply the final reconciliation and explain items the builder did not provide.

angle: Furnished coastal purchases and unit ownership
source_label: City of Destin STR registration guide
local: Use Destin’s registration guide for a property within the city and confirm the actual municipality before applying it to a home marketed as part of the wider Destin area. Save the applicable registration documents separately from the tax study.
scope: A furnished condo acquisition needs an inventory that distinguishes what transferred with the unit from assets owned by the association. A listing photograph may show a pool, boardwalk, and fitness room without establishing any separately allocable ownership cost. Ask for the deed, condo documents, and seller inventory before assigning costs to advertised amenities. Later furniture purchases should reconcile to invoices and the existing fixed-asset ledger.
records: Unit deed, condominium declaration, and closing statement
Seller inventory reconciled to retained and replaced furnishings
Descriptions of association assessments rather than only payment totals
scenario: A unit closes with beds and appliances, then the buyer replaces several pieces. Preserve the acquired inventory and mark the replacements. The study preparer needs to distinguish the purchase allocation from later spending; adding every receipt to an assumed furnished-purchase allowance can overstate the analyzed costs.
question: Can an advertised resort pool go into my unit’s component schedule?
answer: Do not assume it can. Establish ownership and the relevant acquisition documents first. The study scope should explain what is included in the unit interest and how shared property is treated rather than infer ownership from marketing photos.

angle: A corridor of communities rather than a single municipality
local: For a 30A property, start with Walton County’s vacation-rental registration office and identify the parcel’s applicable jurisdiction. The 30A label describes a destination; it should not replace the actual address, parcel, and association documents in a study file.
scope: Large furnished homes can have a closing inventory, separately installed pool equipment, and upgrades ordered between closing and opening. Keep those transactions distinct. Identify whether outdoor living costs describe removable furnishings, installed equipment, or permanent construction. The useful question is how each item was acquired and used, not how much of the purchase a provider promises to accelerate.
records: Parcel identifier and applicable rental-registration records
Seller’s furnishing list with any separately negotiated allocation
Pool equipment, outdoor-kitchen, and post-closing improvement invoices
scenario: A home is purchased furnished and its outdoor kitchen is renovated before guests arrive. The seller’s inventory, acquired building costs, and new contractor work are separate evidence trails. Ask the contractor to distinguish equipment from supporting construction and identify what was removed, retained, or added.
question: Should every expense before the first reservation be one cost pool?
answer: No single booking date explains the nature of all spending. Organize closing costs, acquired contents, repairs, and improvements separately for the preparer to evaluate. Record when each improvement was available for its intended rental use.

angle: Inspection work and building-versus-unit responsibilities
source_label: Panama City Beach short-term rental program
local: Panama City Beach publishes a dedicated STR program page with registration and inspection materials. Confirm that your address is within the city covered by that program before using its documents for an investment timeline.
scope: For a condo upgraded before rental registration, split owner-paid interior work from building-wide association projects. An inspection punch list may describe safety corrections, but it does not automatically establish whether spending is an expense or a capital improvement. Keep the contractor’s invoice, the affected component, and the completion date together so the tax preparer can make that decision before a study incorporates the cost.
records: Unit registration and inspection file
Interior punch-list invoices matched to the work performed
Association notices specifying the purpose of each assessment
scenario: An inspection leads to replacement alarms, electrical work, and a contractor visit that also includes a kitchen upgrade. Request a breakdown of the service visit. Treating the entire payment as one inspection expense or one furnishing asset hides facts the preparer needs.
question: Is an inspection invoice enough to classify an improvement?
answer: It can document why work was requested, but usually does not explain all materials, installation, ownership, or scope. Preserve the invoice and inspection report together and obtain missing detail from the contractor.

angle: Separate property files for separately licensed rentals
local: Gulf Shores directs rental owners to its rental-license process, and its business-license guidance addresses separate locations. Use the property’s actual location to identify the applicable licensing file rather than assuming a neighboring beach community follows the same process.
scope: Owners with more than one beach rental should reconcile furniture and improvements by property. A bulk invoice for mattresses, kitchenware, and patio furniture may serve several units. Mark the destination of each item and document transfers between properties. The study team should not have to infer which unit received an asset from a management-company charge alone.
records: A property-by-property index of closing and licensing records
Bulk purchase invoices allocated to actual receiving properties
Transfer and replacement log for furnishings moved between rentals
scenario: An owner orders furniture for two condos but pays with one business card. Create separate inventory rows with a property identifier, quantity, and invoice reference. Have the bookkeeper reconcile the split to the total payment before giving either condo file to the study provider.
question: Can one study cover several Gulf Shores rentals?
answer: Discuss the engagement scope, but keep each property’s basis, service dates, and supporting schedules distinguishable. A portfolio-level fee should not erase the audit trail for the assets allocated to each address.

angle: A vacation-home rule may not describe a condominium interest
local: Orange Beach’s vacation-rental page identifies a specific dwelling category. Confirm which city requirements apply to your actual dwelling type rather than applying a single-family description to every condominium or resort unit.
scope: For a coastal condo, distinguish a unit owner’s purchases from common-area work, management costs, and association payments. Ask the association for the project description behind a special assessment. A payment labeled roof, reserve, or capital assessment still needs ownership and tax analysis; it should not be converted directly into an assumed short-life component.
records: Ownership declaration and unit boundaries
Assessment notices with scope and funding explanations
Directly owned appliances, furniture, and interior improvement records
scenario: The association renovates a shared deck while the owner installs flooring inside the unit. Maintain separate records even if both payments occur in the same month. The interior invoice can identify unit-specific materials; the assessment requires different documents to explain what was funded and owned.
question: Should recurring association dues enter the study basis?
answer: Do not add operating payments to capital costs automatically. Give the preparer the dues and assessment detail so the nature of each payment can be evaluated before the study team receives an approved basis schedule.

angle: Pool-area projects and equipment packages
local: Scottsdale’s owner/operator page describes its licensing process and supporting compliance information. Use that current city resource for operating requirements; completing a cost segregation study does not satisfy a rental-license requirement.
scope: A resort-style backyard can combine a pool, equipment, barriers, paving, lighting, and movable furniture. Ask contractors to identify those elements in their scopes and supply photographs showing how they are installed. A single backyard renovation total does not tell the study preparer which costs belong to the building, site, or equipment. Avoid treating every outdoor item as the same asset class.
records: Pool and equipment contracts with installation detail
Barrier, lighting, paving, and landscape scopes
Owner inventory identifying furniture versus installed improvements
scenario: An owner adds a pool barrier and replaces outdoor furnishings while upgrading the pool controls. Keep separate invoice lines and completion dates for each project. Record which controls were replaced and ask the tax preparer how to reconcile the old asset record.
question: Does a pool-safety project automatically qualify for accelerated depreciation?
answer: The reason for the project does not decide the asset classification. Document construction, function, ownership, and cost; the preparer can then assess treatment using the applicable authority.

angle: City permitting and distinctive site improvements
local: Sedona’s city FAQ addresses its STR permit and state licensing coordination. Confirm whether the parcel is within the city before applying that guidance to a property marketed under a Sedona-area destination name.
scope: A home with terraces, retaining work, and guest outdoor areas needs construction records describing what each improvement supports. Retaining walls can serve different functions within one parcel. Ask the contractor to identify structural support, access, drainage, and landscaping work rather than sending one site-work number. Preserve a site plan that connects each invoice to an actual location.
records: Site plan with terraces, access, and retaining-work locations
Contractor detail describing each wall’s purpose
Rental-use and owner-use calendar for the home
scenario: A hillside project combines structural stabilization near the house with a separate patio for guests. The same contractor may build both. Separate the scopes and costs so the study does not assume that every wall or paved surface has identical tax treatment.
question: Can a landscaping invoice support every outdoor asset?
answer: Only if its detail actually describes the items and costs being analyzed. Request a breakdown for significant bundled construction and keep photographs showing attachment and function. Generic invoice labels leave assumptions unresolved.

angle: Jurisdiction, multiple structures, and furnished-unit scope
local: Austin provides an STR licensing guide and directs owners to current city requirements. Confirm the jurisdiction and unit covered by the application before treating a guesthouse, accessory structure, and main residence as one operating property.
scope: For a property with a main home and a guest unit, draw a use map showing guest-only, owner-only, and shared areas. Separate appliances dedicated to the rental from whole-property systems. Have the return preparer establish the appropriate business-use and basis treatment before the study allocates individual components. The presence of a separate entrance does not, by itself, resolve those questions.
records: Floor plan labeling each structure and its actual use
Invoices identifying which unit received the improvement
Ownership, conversion, and rental-availability timeline
scenario: An owner lives in the main house and furnishes a backyard unit. A landscaping project also improves the shared yard. Identify the dedicated furniture separately and explain the shared project to the preparer instead of assigning all yard spending to the guest unit.
question: Should I use the whole purchase price for a guesthouse estimate?
answer: First establish the study scope and applicable basis allocation. Provide the main-home and guest-unit facts so the preparer can determine which property costs belong in the analysis.

angle: Permit identity and multi-unit property records
local: Nashville’s permit application page identifies its documentation process. Match the proposed study property to the actual permitted address and unit; an advertised neighborhood name or a developer’s projected use is not an operating authorization.
scope: For a townhouse or multi-unit purchase, identify which interiors, parking spaces, and common elements are actually included in the ownership interest. Developer packages may combine construction and optional furnishings. Obtain the final option sheet and closing adjustments so the study does not add a furniture package already included in the total acquisition costs.
records: Unit deed and any shared-element declaration
Developer option sheet reconciled to closing adjustments
Furniture package invoice with included and excluded items
scenario: A buyer chooses a turnkey furnishing package from the developer and later buys extra beds. Compare the option-sheet charge with the closing statement, then record the later invoice separately. Treating the developer package as an additional cost without checking the settlement totals can count it twice.
question: Does a turnkey purchase eliminate the need for an inventory?
answer: No. Turnkey describes the offering, not the supporting tax records. Ask for a list of transferred items and a reconciliation to the transaction documents so the study provider can understand what the purchase included.

angle: Desert parcels, accessory spaces, and site function
source_label: San Bernardino County STR land-use guidance
local: San Bernardino County’s land-use service explains the regions and zoning designations addressed by its STR rules. Use the actual parcel and zoning when checking a Joshua Tree-area property; proximity to the park does not establish the applicable land-use approval.
scope: Desert guest properties may have detached spaces, shade structures, outdoor bathing equipment, fencing, and substantial site work. Document each item’s installation and use instead of assigning one guest-experience allowance. Identify any structure excluded from the rental and distinguish nondepreciable land from separately documented improvements. Ask for photographs from before and after a renovation when existing structures were altered.
records: Parcel map identifying structures included in the rental scope
Shade, fence, equipment, and site-work contracts
Pre-renovation photographs and a retained/replaced asset list
scenario: A buyer adds a freestanding shade structure, outdoor seating, and electrical work to an existing home. The furnishings, structural work, and equipment connections should be described individually. An invoice called outdoor lounge is insufficient to explain how its components function.
question: Can guest-experience upgrades all use one recovery period?
answer: No such conclusion follows from the marketing description. The study must evaluate the physical components and supporting costs. Separate removable items from construction and identify which assets serve the building generally.

angle: Vacation-rental registration and design-led remodels
local: Palm Springs maintains a dedicated vacation-rental program with governing documents and registration information. Confirm the intended operating category and address-specific eligibility before building an acquisition model around short stays.
scope: A design-led remodel can combine removable furniture, decorative features, custom cabinetry, and changes to the permanent building. Request an itemized designer procurement schedule and contractor scope. Preserve which items were acquired with the home and which were bought later. A design budget should not be used as a substitute for component costs merely because everything contributes to the same visual style.
records: Acquired inventory and later designer purchase schedule
Construction drawings distinguishing permanent work from furnishing installation
Pool, patio, and interior scopes reconciled to total project spending
scenario: A remodel introduces custom built-ins and freestanding pieces with matching finishes. They may look like one furniture collection in photographs, yet have different installation and function. Give the preparer separate invoices and attachment details before using a designer’s category labels in the asset schedule.
question: Does midcentury style change the study methodology?
answer: Style is not the basis for an asset classification. A useful study records actual construction, use, cost, and ownership. Supply the details behind custom work even when the property’s marketing groups it all under a single design concept.

angle: Big Bear Lake city versus surrounding county property
local: Big Bear Lake publishes city vacation-rental resources. Verify whether the parcel falls inside that city or an unincorporated county area before relying on the city program; the broader Big Bear destination name covers more than one jurisdiction.
scope: For a cabin renovated in stages, reconstruct the acquisition and improvement history before ordering the study. A replaced heater, new game-room furnishings, and an expanded deck may have different service dates and ownership records. Match later work to the original ledger so the study provider can identify what remains in use rather than assigning a current replacement cost to every visible item.
records: City/county parcel identification
Historical asset schedule with replaced items marked
Separate game-room, deck, and building-system invoices
scenario: A cabin operates for several winters before the owner remodels its game room. The new table and electronics are supported by purchase receipts, while changes to the room need contractor detail. Keep both sets separate from the acquisition file and note items removed from service.
question: Can current photos replace older improvement invoices?
answer: Photos can help identify what exists, but they do not establish every historical cost or service date. Explain missing records to the study provider and preserve the assumptions used to address them.

angle: A regional name spanning several jurisdictions
local: Placer County’s program is a starting point for parcels in its applicable North Lake Tahoe area; it is not a basin-wide rulebook. Confirm the state, county, and municipality for the actual address before relying on a Tahoe rental-permit guide.
scope: For a condominium or mountain home, first define the ownership interest and personal-use pattern. A ski-area condo may include shared amenities and a management arrangement, while a standalone home has separate site costs. Do not combine the two models in an estimate. Bring the governing documents and the exact inventory of owner assets so the study scope matches what the taxpayer owns.
records: State, county, and municipal parcel identification
Condo declaration or standalone-property site plan
Owner-use calendar and the manager’s asset inventory
scenario: Two properties both advertise a Lake Tahoe address, but one is a condo and the other a separate home. Prepare independent basis and ownership schedules. A reclassification assumption from one property is not evidence for the other, even when the acquisition prices are similar.
question: Does a Tahoe market estimate apply across the entire basin?
answer: It should not be treated that way. Costs, ownership, operating rules, and rental use vary by parcel. Request a property-specific scope and identify the jurisdiction rather than relying on a regional average.

angle: License zones and association-managed mountain units
local: Breckenridge publishes accommodation-license information, including caps and zones. Check the applicable zone and current licensing position directly with the town before using expected STR operation as an assumption in a study feasibility discussion.
scope: For a resort condo, obtain the unit deed, association documents, and management contract. Identify whether a furnishing refresh was purchased by the owner, funded through an assessment, or retained by an operator. Those arrangements can change the records needed to define the study. Keep the operating license and management agreement separate from the component-cost evidence.
records: Address and applicable accommodation-license category
Unit ownership documents and management agreement
Furniture-refresh invoices identifying purchaser and owner
scenario: A rental manager replaces a furnishing package and deducts the cost from owner distributions. Obtain the underlying vendor detail and reconcile the deduction to the owner ledger. A net distribution statement alone does not explain what assets were acquired or which unit received them.
question: Can my manager’s annual statement be the full asset file?
answer: Usually it needs supporting detail. Ask for invoices, inventory changes, and project dates that reconcile to the statement. The study provider should be able to identify the actual items behind capital charges.

angle: Nightly-rental identity and lockout-unit boundaries
source_label: Park City building permits and nightly-rental licensing
local: Park City’s building-permit page identifies nightly-rental licensing as a separate requirement. Confirm the city boundary and the approved unit configuration before equating a resort marketing description with the property covered by an operating license.
scope: A lockout condo can function as connected space or separate guest areas. Supply a floor plan and explain actual use, shared systems, and ownership. Reconcile furnishing packages by unit or area instead of assuming separate booking listings mean separate tax assets. The study and return preparer need consistent property identifiers across acquisition, management, and depreciation records.
records: Floor plan identifying lockout doors and shared spaces
Deed and condominium declaration for the ownership interest
Unit-level inventory and management booking identifiers
scenario: A buyer acquires one deeded condo but the manager advertises two lockout listings. Create an inventory that maps each item to the relevant room and reconciles to the one acquisition. Explain shared appliances and systems rather than treating the two listings as two independent purchases.
question: Does a separate booking listing establish separate property basis?
answer: No. Start with the transaction and ownership documents, then map the rental configuration. Booking identifiers are operational records; they do not independently establish tax ownership or acquisition cost.

angle: Owner-adjacent units and shared building costs
local: Boston’s STR program distinguishes operating categories and addresses owner-adjacent registrations. Confirm the applicable category and actual unit before assuming a furnished Boston purchase can operate as an unrestricted whole-home vacation rental.
scope: For an owner-occupied multifamily building, map each unit and the common systems before allocating costs. An owner’s kitchen remodel should not flow into the guest-unit inventory. A shared roof or heating project needs a separate allocation discussion with the preparer. Keep rental-unit assets, owner-space improvements, and building-wide projects distinguishable in both bookkeeping and the study request.
records: Unit floor plans and actual owner/rental use
Invoices labeled by unit or common building area
Registration category and prior depreciation records
scenario: The owner lives on one floor and furnishes another unit for guests. A plumbing contractor works in both units during one visit. Ask for labor and materials identified by work area; splitting the total equally without factual support can obscure the proper scope.
question: Can the entire building go into an STR estimate?
answer: Only after the scope and applicable use allocation are resolved. Provide the property’s mixed-use facts and have the preparer establish the basis to analyze before component reclassification begins.

angle: Legal hosting model before furnished-property assumptions
source_label: NYC Office of Special Enforcement registration law
local: New York City’s Office of Special Enforcement explains its short-term rental registration framework and exemptions. Verify the lawful hosting model and building status before evaluating a purchase as an STR investment; registration is not a blanket authorization for every furnished apartment.
scope: Define whether the taxpayer owns the building, a condominium interest, or only furnishings in leased space. A tenant furnishing a room cannot simply commission a study of the landlord’s building basis. For an owned unit with personal use, document the actual guest space and shared areas. Discuss any cooperative interest or unusual ownership form directly with the preparer before assuming a conventional building study fits.
records: Deed, lease, or ownership documents establishing the taxpayer’s interest
Floor plan of guest, personal, and shared areas
Furniture receipts and any landlord-funded work agreements
scenario: A host leases an apartment and buys furniture. The apartment’s market value is not the host’s building basis. The preparer should evaluate the host-owned assets and any tenant improvements within the actual ownership and lease terms instead of using a whole-apartment purchase model.
question: Does furnishing an apartment create building basis for the host?
answer: No. The underlying ownership and spending facts must support what is analyzed. Identify assets the host actually owns and review the lease before requesting a building-level cost segregation proposal.

angle: STRO categories and room-versus-whole-home use
source_label: San Diego short-term residential occupancy program
local: San Diego’s STRO page distinguishes several hosting categories, including home sharing and whole-home use. Match the licensing and use facts to the particular unit before making a study request; other San Diego County cities have their own jurisdictional context.
scope: For a home-sharing arrangement, identify guest-only rooms, shared living areas, and owner-only space. For a whole-home rental, reconcile any personal-use periods and later changes in operation. The component inventory should describe dedicated rental furnishings separately from shared building assets. An operating category informs the fact file but does not determine federal depreciation treatment by itself.
records: Applicable STRO category and unit identifier
Guest/owner use map and rental calendar
Dedicated furnishing receipts plus shared-improvement scopes
scenario: A homeowner rents rooms for part of the year and later offers the entire home while away. Keep a dated operating timeline and identify any furnishings added for the changed use. Do not assume that one year-end photograph accurately describes rental use throughout the year.
question: Does an STRO tier settle the federal tax classification?
answer: No. City licensing and federal tax rules answer different questions. Provide the operating facts and use history so the preparer can evaluate the appropriate tax treatment separately.

angle: Primary-residence operation and personal-use boundaries
local: Denver’s zoning use limitations address short-term rentals in connection with primary residence. Confirm the current licensing and zoning treatment for the parcel before evaluating a separate investment property as though every residential address allows the same STR use.
scope: A primary-residence rental needs a clearly documented use history. Identify rooms available to guests, periods of personal occupancy, and improvements made specifically to the rental area. Ask the preparer to resolve the business-use and conversion facts before the study provider works from a whole-home basis. Owner occupancy is not a detail that can be added after the estimate is finished.
records: Guest and personal-use calendar
Floor plan showing shared and exclusive spaces
Original acquisition documents and conversion-related valuation support if applicable
scenario: A homeowner finishes a guest room and replaces the home’s roof in the same year. The guest-room furniture and whole-building roof are different projects with different allocation questions. Document both rather than putting all spending into a single STR launch budget.
question: Can a primary residence still merit a property review?
answer: Possibly, but feasibility starts with the eligible scope and the owner’s facts. A limited rental area or personal-use pattern can materially change the analysis. Have the preparer establish that scope before requesting a full-building projection.

angle: Permit categories and historic-building renovations
local: Charleston provides category criteria for its STR permits. Use the city’s criteria and the property’s actual location when confirming the operating model; a nearby beach town or county address should not be evaluated under a Charleston-city category by default.
scope: For an older building with later guest accommodations, separate original building costs from subsequent interior renovations and owner-purchased furnishings. Architectural character does not determine a recovery period. Retain plans explaining permanent partitions and systems, especially when invoices use broad restoration descriptions. The preparer needs to understand what was repaired, replaced, or newly added before approving costs for the study.
records: Property identity and applicable permit category
Renovation plans with original and new work distinguished
Itemized restoration invoices and furnishing purchase records
scenario: A contractor restores interior finishes while a designer supplies removable guest furnishings. The combined project budget describes the guest experience but does not explain the individual assets. Reconcile the contractor and designer files separately, then tie them to the owner’s capitalized costs.
question: Does historic character justify a special reclassification percentage?
answer: No market-wide percentage follows from a building’s age or style. A report should support the actual component costs and functions. Ask for the reasoning behind classifications rather than a promised outcome based on the neighborhood.

angle: STVR approval and carriage-house ownership scope
local: Savannah’s STVR program describes its application and planning process. Check the actual address and dwelling configuration through that program before assuming a carriage house, garden unit, and main home have identical operating treatment.
scope: A property with multiple structures needs a cost map. Identify the main residence, any guest carriage house, shared courtyard, and utilities serving more than one building. Keep improvements paid by a tenant or manager separate from the owner’s costs. The study scope should explain which structures and interests are included and how shared projects will be handled.
records: Site and floor plans showing separate structures
Invoices matched to the main home, guest unit, or shared area
Ownership and management documents for the rented space
scenario: An owner renovates a carriage house while repaving a courtyard used by both buildings. Separate the interior project from the shared site work. Document the use of each area so the preparer can address the allocation instead of assigning the entire property project to the guest unit.
question: Does a separate entrance establish a separate study property?
answer: It helps describe the layout but does not settle ownership or basis. Use the deed, plans, and cost records to define the interest being studied, then explain the actual guest use.

angle: Homestay versus whole-dwelling vacation use
local: Asheville’s homestay page distinguishes renting rooms in a home from short-term vacation rental of an entire dwelling. Confirm which use is permitted at the address rather than assuming the city and surrounding mountain communities share the same rules.
scope: For a homestay, document guest bedrooms and any spaces shared with the household. A project that improves the entire home needs different allocation support from furniture purchased exclusively for the guest rooms. Preserve the personal-use history and discuss the intended scope before obtaining a provider’s benefit estimate. The city’s use terminology should not substitute for a federal tax analysis.
records: Homestay configuration and current operating documents
Room-by-room use map
Guest furnishing invoices separated from whole-home improvement spending
scenario: A homeowner updates two guest bedrooms and also renovates the family kitchen. The interior designer’s invoice covers both areas. Ask for an itemized room allocation based on actual work and purchases so the preparer can evaluate the projects separately.
question: Can I apply a mountain-cabin estimate to an Asheville homestay?
answer: That would overlook meaningful differences in use and scope. A dedicated vacation cabin and rooms in a personal residence may require different basis and allocation analysis. Start with the actual layout and operating pattern.

angle: County identity and coastal improvement records
local: Dare County provides occupancy-tax information for its jurisdiction. The Outer Banks is a regional destination, so first identify the county and municipality for the parcel; Dare’s resource should not be treated as covering every Outer Banks address.
scope: For a coastal home, keep acquisition costs, later exterior work, and any insured repair project separately traceable. Decks, access walks, pools, and structural work may appear in a combined contractor package. Ask for the physical scope and identify reimbursements or credits for the tax preparer to reconcile before the study allocates the property’s costs.
records: County and municipal parcel identification
Exterior project scopes with structural and access work separated
Insurance, reimbursement, and contractor records if a loss-related project occurred
scenario: After acquiring a rental, an owner replaces portions of exterior access and adds new patio furniture. A later insurance-funded repair changes another area. Preserve three distinct records rather than using the final appearance of the property to reconstruct a single acquisition inventory.
question: Are lodging-tax records enough to support depreciation costs?
answer: They help document operations, but they do not establish component basis. Keep the occupancy-tax file alongside, rather than in place of, the closing documents, invoices, and asset history needed for the study.

angle: City home sharing versus regional vacation-home marketing
local: Orlando’s city home-sharing program addresses renting part of a resident’s home while the resident is present. A vacation home advertised as near Orlando may be in a different jurisdiction. Identify the actual address before applying city home-sharing guidance to a whole-home investment.
scope: Scope an owner-occupied home share differently from a dedicated resort home. Document guest-only rooms and shared spaces for the former; obtain association and furnishing records for the latter. A metropolitan marketing label cannot resolve that distinction. The study provider needs the actual property configuration and ownership facts before selecting an inspection or costing approach.
records: Exact city/county jurisdiction and operating category
Room-use map or association ownership documents as applicable
Furnishing and renovation invoices tied to the actual property
scenario: An investor compares a room-rental arrangement inside Orlando with a resort home outside the city. Do not carry the same permit assumptions or whole-property basis model between them. Prepare a separate fact file for each proposal and resolve permitted use before comparing study economics.
question: Is every Orlando-area vacation home governed by the city’s home-sharing rules?
answer: No regional label can answer that. Establish the actual municipality and county, then consult the relevant authority. Use that confirmed operating model when discussing the study scope and tax treatment.

angle: County overlay checks and themed-room invoices
local: Osceola County publishes information about STR planned-development zoning and its overlay map. Confirm whether county or city jurisdiction governs the specific Kissimmee-area parcel before relying on that map for an operating decision.
scope: Themed rooms can combine freestanding beds, electronics, specialty lighting, permanent framing, and custom millwork. Obtain the designer’s procurement list and the builder’s installation detail. A single invoice for a themed bedroom can hide costs already included in the property purchase or items owned by a resort association. Reconcile the package to the owner’s ledger before the study begins.
records: Jurisdiction and applicable zoning confirmation
Designer item list with separate materials and installation scopes
Seller furnishings and newly purchased items reconciled by room
scenario: A room package includes a freestanding bunk bed and a permanently constructed play feature. Photos show the final theme, but invoices need to explain attachment, function, and cost. The study provider should analyze those components separately rather than classify the theme as one asset.
question: Does calling a room furniture make all of its construction furniture?
answer: No. Vendor marketing categories do not replace component analysis. Ask for enough detail to distinguish movable contents from structural and installed work before proposing a recovery classification.

angle: Township-specific operating files and community amenities
local: Pocono Township publishes a transient-dwelling ordinance. It is one township’s code, not a rulebook for the entire Poconos region. Identify the actual township and community association before treating a regional listing description as evidence of rental eligibility.
scope: For a home in an amenity community, distinguish owner assets from community pools, lakeside facilities, roads, and recreational amenities. Association dues and access rights should not become assumed physical assets in the home’s study. Ask for the deed and community documents along with the inventory and any owner-paid exterior improvement invoices.
records: Township identity and community association documents
Owner-versus-association amenity inventory
Home improvement invoices and existing depreciation ledger
scenario: A listing emphasizes a community pool and private guest hot tub. The owner needs to document the hot tub purchase separately and establish what, if anything, the ownership interest includes in shared amenities. A listing feature list does not supply a basis allocation.
question: Can I use one township’s rules for all Poconos properties?
answer: No. Confirm the actual municipality and association for each address. Keep that operating check separate from the component study, which still depends on ownership and cost evidence for the specific home.

angle: Property-specific approval and reconstruction history
local: Maui County maintains separate resources for different short-term rental property categories. Check the actual unit, approval history, and current operating status through those resources before relying on a seller’s historical rental listing.
scope: For a unit that has undergone repairs or reconstruction, assemble a dated asset history rather than only a current inventory. Separate original acquisition, later owner improvements, association work, and any reimbursements. Ask the return preparer to reconcile loss-related adjustments and prior deductions before the study provider uses a basis total. A newly completed interior does not erase the earlier tax history.
records: Unit approval and ownership records
Original schedules plus repair/reconstruction scopes
Association work detail and reimbursement records where applicable
scenario: An owner replaces unit interiors while the association repairs common systems. Preserve separate records for both projects and explain any insurance funding. The study team should work from a reconciled owner-cost schedule, not simply the sum of every repair document in the file.
question: Should a reconstruction study start from the current property value?
answer: Do not substitute current value for a reconciled basis without the preparer’s analysis. Supply the acquisition and subsequent adjustment history so the study can use a supported cost pool.

angle: Parcel identification and outdoor living improvements
source_label: Kauai County transient vacation rental resources
local: Kauai County’s TVR page links approved-property and renewal resources using parcel identifiers. Match the property’s tax map key and approval records to the interest being acquired rather than relying solely on a vacation-rental name.
scope: A furnished home with lanais, covered outdoor areas, and detached storage requires a clear installation and use inventory. Removable outdoor furniture should be distinguished from roofs, structural supports, and other permanent construction. Identify owner storage and personal-use areas before allocating costs. Ask the study provider how the site plan and component photographs will support the scope.
records: Tax map key and matching ownership/approval file
Lanai and detached-structure plans
Outdoor furnishing receipts and owner-use records
scenario: A renovation adds new seating and a permanent roof over an outdoor living area. They may appear together on one designer budget, but the construction and furniture evidence should be separated. Retain the contractor scope describing attachment and structural support.
question: Does outdoor placement imply a shorter asset life?
answer: No. Location outdoors does not explain function, permanence, or ownership. Document the individual components and let the study and tax preparer evaluate their treatment.

angle: County lodging records and cabin site-work packages
source_label: Fannin County lodging-tax and STR resources
local: Fannin County’s lodging-tax page links its STR materials. Determine whether the cabin falls under the county or a city authority before using that resource for the operating file; the Blue Ridge destination label alone is not enough.
scope: For a cabin with access-road work, retaining improvements, a deck, and a hot tub, identify the purpose of each project. Site contractors may combine grading that supports the building with other improvements. Request cost detail and photographs showing where the work occurred. Keep maintenance spending and capital-project records separate for the preparer’s review before the study team receives its scope.
records: Parcel jurisdiction and lodging-account file
Access, grading, retaining, and deck construction scopes
Hot-tub and equipment invoices tied to installation dates
scenario: A single excavation invoice covers a building pad and a guest parking area. Ask for quantities or other factual detail supporting the split. A generic site-improvement percentage would hide the different functions that the study needs to evaluate.
question: Can all grading costs be called land improvements?
answer: Not automatically. Explain what the work supports and how the costs were developed. Land, building-support work, and other improvements need fact-specific treatment rather than a label chosen from the invoice title.

angle: Nightly-rental eligibility and manager-supplied furnishings
local: Branson publishes an STR program page and an address-based nightly-rental zoning tool. Confirm the address and applicable jurisdiction before treating a resort-area listing as evidence that a particular unit can operate under the city’s program.
scope: For a condo placed into a management program, determine who owns the furnishings and pays for refreshes. Management deductions may bundle repairs, linen purchases, furniture, and operating charges. Request supporting invoices and an inventory that maps items to the unit. The study should reconcile owner assets rather than infer a complete furniture package from a net payout statement.
records: Address-specific operating and ownership records
Management agreement identifying asset ownership
Vendor invoices underlying furniture-refresh deductions
scenario: A manager withholds funds for a unit refresh and the owner buys additional furniture directly. Match the manager’s purchases to vendor invoices, then compare them with the owner’s receipts. This avoids treating the same delivered items as both a management charge and a separate acquisition.
question: Can management charges replace an itemized asset inventory?
answer: They can help reconcile payments, but they do not always identify the assets or their owner. Obtain item descriptions, dates, and unit assignments before using the charges in a study.

angle: Separate the casita from the rooms you occupy
local: Albuquerque’s FAQ distinguishes entire homes, rooms, and accessory units such as casitas, subject to zoning approval. Match the floor plan in the operating file to the spaces actually offered to guests.
scope: A detached casita can share a utility connection, driveway, or landscaped courtyard with the owner’s home. Mark exclusive guest space and shared facilities on a site sketch. Give the preparer the cost records for each structure and explain how the spaces are used; do not apply the rental unit’s furnishing list to the entire parcel.
records: Casita and main-house floor plans
Utility extension invoices and courtyard work descriptions
Rental calendar with owner-use notes
scenario: An owner converts a workshop into a guest casita while continuing to live in the main house. The conversion invoice includes a service-panel upgrade serving both buildings. Identify that shared work separately from the kitchenette equipment so the provider can evaluate the allocation.
question: Does a separate guest entrance establish a separate tax asset?
answer: An entrance helps describe the layout but does not resolve ownership, basis, or allocation. Show the actual construction and use of the rooms, including connections to the main house.

angle: Match island jurisdiction and inspection work to the acquired property
source_label: City of Anna Maria vacation rentals
local: The City of Anna Maria publishes registration and inspection procedures for vacation rentals. This city resource is not an island-wide approval: first identify the municipality responsible for the property.
scope: For a furnished coastal home, distinguish assets acquired with the house from safety work completed for opening. A seller’s listing photographs may show items removed before closing. Record what was delivered, what failed inspection, and what you replaced. Keep pool equipment, alarms, and structural repairs in separate invoice lines for the study discussion.
records: Closing inventory checked against possession-day photographs
Inspection findings and contractor completion records
Pool and safety-equipment receipts with installation details
scenario: A sale includes a pool heater, but it fails before the first booking and is replaced. Preserve evidence of the acquired heater and the new invoice rather than presenting both as two operating heaters in the current inventory.
question: Can an inspection checklist replace a furnishing inventory?
answer: No. An inspection addresses operating conditions. A room-by-room inventory identifies the assets you received and the evidence supporting their costs; both can belong in the file.

angle: Condo-hotel management does not establish ownership of every amenity
source_label: Aspen STR permit types and program guidance
local: Aspen distinguishes lodging-exempt, owner-occupied, and classic STR permits. Its guidance explains that a condo-hotel manager and an individual unit owner can have different application paths.
scope: Before studying a managed unit, separate the deeded interior from amenities controlled by the association or operator. Obtain the furnishing-package agreement, reserve statements, and any mandatory refurbishment charges. Ask the provider to identify costs attributable to your ownership interest rather than assigning a share of every facility advertised by the resort.
records: Unit deed and condominium declaration
Operator furnishing schedule and replacement-reserve ledger
Refurbishment invoices distinguishing unit and common work
scenario: A manager deducts a reserve contribution each month and later replaces bedroom furniture. The contribution and the furniture purchase are not two separate acquisitions. Request the underlying purchase detail and the ownership arrangement before adding either to a study schedule.
question: Does a lodge-wide permit tell me which assets my unit owns?
answer: No. Permit coverage describes operations. Title documents and management agreements determine the property interests and contractual obligations the preparer needs to evaluate.

angle: Keep the primary residence and additional unit in separate study files
local: Atlanta’s program discusses a primary residence and an additional dwelling, and provides a city-boundary property lookup. Establish which addresses are within Atlanta before relying on its licensing process.
scope: One operator account can conceal very different property histories. A residence used occasionally by guests, an acquired rental, and a tenant-furnished unit should not receive a single pooled basis calculation. Record ownership, exclusive rental areas, and improvements by address. Have the return preparer resolve owner-versus-tenant costs before requesting a provider estimate.
records: Property-by-property title or lease record
Residence-use calendar and room measurements
Separate acquisition and improvement ledgers
scenario: An owner buys furniture for both a primary residence and a second rental on one invoice. Annotate delivery destinations and allocate delivery charges using a documented method. The total card charge alone cannot show which property received each item.
question: Can I use one furnishing allowance for both addresses?
answer: Only after reconciling the actual items and costs for each. A shared vendor or listing account does not make the buildings or ownership interests interchangeable.

angle: Document hosted rooms without treating the whole rowhouse as guest space
local: Baltimore’s licensing FAQ discusses hosted short-term stays and permanent-residence requirements. Confirm the current license category with the city and retain the application’s description of the rented space.
scope: For a rowhouse with guest bedrooms, map the rooms rented exclusively, common circulation, and owner-only areas. Renovations to stairs, plumbing, or the roof may serve the whole house, while particular furnishings serve the guest rooms. Present those differences explicitly instead of valuing everything visible in listing photographs as rental property.
records: Floor plan identifying private and shared rooms
Guest-room inventory with purchase dates
Whole-house and room-specific renovation invoices
scenario: A host replaces a shared hallway floor and buys beds for two rental rooms. The beds have identifiable locations; the hallway serves both guests and occupants. Keep those facts distinct when the preparer evaluates the rental allocation.
question: Does hosted status settle the deduction calculation?
answer: No. Local license terminology does not establish federal depreciation or personal-use treatment. Supply actual room use, dates, and costs to the return preparer.

angle: Reconcile a change from year-round tenants to short stays
source_label: Bend STR permits and operating licenses
local: Bend publishes separate information about short-term rental permits and operating licenses, including renewal documentation. Save the approvals applicable to your address and the dates of any operating change.
scope: A previously leased home may already have an asset schedule before it is furnished for vacation guests. Start with that schedule and a transition timeline. Distinguish existing building components from newly purchased furniture and turnover projects. Ask how the provider will reconcile prior depreciation instead of treating the conversion as a new purchase of the house.
records: Last long-term lease and transition calendar
Existing depreciation schedule and earlier improvements
Furnishing invoices and turnover-project cost detail
scenario: A twelve-month tenancy ends and the owner adds laundry equipment before accepting nightly reservations. The house acquisition date has not changed. Record the equipment addition separately and identify the interval when work prevented the property from being ready for guests.
question: Is the operating-license date the purchase date for the study?
answer: No. Licensing, acquisition, and readiness for use are different events. Give the preparer the evidence for each rather than selecting one date for every asset.

angle: Track furnishings across an accessory unit and the main house
local: Boise publishes its STR licensing framework through the city. Check the current application and permitted use for the specific dwelling; a postal address alone does not describe which rooms are rented.
scope: If an owner moves furniture from a personal residence into a guest unit, purchase price, transfer date, and condition become separate pieces of evidence. Mark transferred items rather than mixing them into a new retail furnishing package. Ask the preparer to address conversion treatment and any missing records before the provider builds its component schedule.
records: Original receipts for transferred furniture where available
Dated guest-unit inventory and condition photographs
New purchases separated from personally used items
scenario: A sofa purchased years earlier moves into a guest suite while new bedroom furniture arrives from a retailer. A spreadsheet showing today’s replacement prices for both is not a record of what the owner paid or when each item entered rental use.
question: Can a current online price support every furniture value?
answer: It may provide context, but it is not proof of the historical transaction or conversion basis. Label estimates and missing evidence so the preparer can resolve the valuation approach.

angle: Identify cabin structures, land work, and the actual operating jurisdiction
source_label: City of Broken Bow official website
local: Use the City of Broken Bow’s official resources to establish the relevant city contact. A cabin marketed as a Broken Bow getaway may require a different jurisdictional inquiry; verify the parcel before selecting permit records.
scope: A cabin project can include a steep access drive, utility runs, clearing, a detached game building, and the main residence. Request a site plan and contractor breakdown by physical improvement. Do not assign the entire site-preparation bill to the cabin shell or assume every outdoor expenditure has the same depreciation treatment.
records: Parcel map and a labeled site plan
Earthwork and utility invoices with location descriptions
Main cabin and detached-building completion records
scenario: A builder invoices a driveway, buried electric service, and a game-room foundation as one exterior package. Ask for quantities or subcontractor detail. The study needs to distinguish what was constructed and what each element serves before classifications can be supported.
question: Does the rental listing’s market name identify the permit authority?
answer: No. Use the parcel location and governmental boundary, then confirm the applicable office directly. Marketing descriptions are useful for guests but are not jurisdiction evidence.

angle: Separate the rental calendar from seasonal property work
local: Cannon Beach publishes a specific 14-day permit resource. Review the permit actually held rather than assuming all vacation homes operate under identical booking conditions.
scope: For a home used by both owners and paying guests, preserve the calendar alongside maintenance and renovation dates. Explain which work made the property unavailable and which work occurred between reservations. A seasonal gap in bookings is not enough to determine how the property or each improvement was used.
records: Permit category and booking history
Owner-use and maintenance calendar
Exterior work invoices and dated completion photographs
scenario: A cottage receives new window coverings during a spring owner stay and deck repairs before summer rentals. Keep separate descriptions, costs, and dates; the owner’s single seasonal spending total does not explain either project’s function or use.
question: Can the rental permit determine my personal-use allocation?
answer: No. Keep actual use records for the return preparer. Local limits on reservations and federal rules for a dwelling used as a home answer different questions.

angle: Build a town-specific file for a seasonal cottage purchase
local: Barnstable’s Health Division provides rental-registration information. Use it for a Barnstable property, then check the appropriate town for a cottage elsewhere on Cape Cod; the regional destination name is not a single permitting jurisdiction.
scope: A seasonal cottage acquisition may include outbuildings, exterior showers, furnishings, and later winterization work. Prepare a closing inventory before contractors remove old items. Record the function and location of plumbing work rather than describing the entire project as a vacation-rental upgrade.
records: Town and parcel identification with registration file
Closing inventory including exterior equipment
Winterization contract and plumbing scope by location
scenario: A buyer acquires a furnished summer cottage, replaces its outdoor shower, and adds year-round heating. Treat the acquired assets and the two later projects as distinct evidence groups. The provider can then reconcile costs without assuming every component was purchased at closing.
question: Does regional tourism registration replace town records?
answer: No. Identify the town responsible for the parcel and retain its applicable records. Use acquisition documents, not registration fees or tourism descriptions, to support the study’s cost reconciliation.

angle: Reconcile county records with a renovated rental’s actual configuration
source_label: Mecklenburg County Office of Tax Administration
local: Mecklenburg County’s Office of Tax Administration handles real and personal property valuation. Its records are a useful starting point for identifying the parcel behind a Charlotte rental purchase.
scope: Compare the recorded building description with your survey, floor plan, and renovation history. A recently finished room or converted garage may not be apparent in an older property record. Give the provider the discrepancy and supporting documents instead of silently using whichever square footage creates a larger allocation.
records: County property record and closing survey
Before-and-after plans for converted areas
Contractor ledger matched to each renovation phase
scenario: A purchased home is advertised with a finished garage studio, while an older record describes an unfinished garage. Supply plans and permits showing what existed at acquisition and distinguish the buyer’s later furnishing purchases from the seller’s construction.
question: Is the assessed building value the cost segregation basis?
answer: Not automatically. The preparer must reconcile the owner’s transaction and tax records. Assessment information can help describe the property but does not replace that calculation.

angle: Tie a waterfront acquisition to the unit and improvements actually owned
source_label: City of Chelan STR license information
local: Chelan’s city licensing page includes zoning, inspection, and ownership-change information. Determine whether the rental is within the city before applying that process to a lake-area address.
scope: For a property sold with waterfront access, separate deeded improvements from shared facilities and use rights. A listing may advertise a dock, beach, or launch that the owner does not hold individually. Supply recorded agreements and explain any improvement payments before the provider assigns costs to those amenities.
records: Deed and waterfront easement or shared-use agreement
Dock or shore-improvement invoices identifying ownership
Closing cost allocation and possession inventory
scenario: A townhouse purchase includes the right to use an association dock, and the new owner also buys patio furniture. The dock’s presence in the listing does not make it a separately acquired owner-controlled asset comparable to the patio set.
question: Should I allocate a percentage of every shared amenity to my unit?
answer: First establish the ownership and payment arrangement. Have the preparer evaluate the documents rather than applying a percentage derived from guest access or marketing photographs.

angle: Keep shared-housing registration and building ownership distinct
local: Chicago’s shared-housing code addresses registration for each dwelling unit and zoning review. Use the registered unit identifier to align the operating file with the physical space in the study.
scope: For a two-flat or small apartment building, separate unit interiors from a common boiler, stairs, roof, and laundry room. Identify which units are rented nightly, leased longer term, or owner occupied. The building’s systems should be traced to the areas served rather than copied into every unit inventory.
records: Unit schedule showing rental and owner use
Common-system diagrams or contractor descriptions
Building acquisition file and unit-level furnishing lists
scenario: A landlord furnishes an upper unit for visitors while keeping a lower unit on an annual lease. The shared boiler replacement appears once in the building file; the new beds appear in the upper-unit file. This prevents a repeated whole-building cost in each rental schedule.
question: Does each registration require a separate valuation of the entire building?
answer: No. Ask the provider to define the reporting scope and reconcile shared costs. Multiple operating units should not cause the same acquired component to be counted repeatedly.

angle: Trace furnishings and common costs through a duplex turnover
local: Cincinnati’s Finance Department provides STR registration information and instructions for displaying the registration identifier. Align that identifier with the address and unit number in your acquisition records.
scope: A duplex can transition one floor at a time. Keep the continuing tenant’s area, newly furnished rooms, and shared basement equipment identifiable. Give the provider a unit schedule showing which costs belong to a particular floor and which serve the entire building. Ask the preparer how prior depreciation connects to the new report.
records: Unit-by-unit lease and guest-use timeline
Furniture delivery records with unit labels
Shared basement and utility-system invoices
scenario: An owner buys two identical washer-dryer sets, one for a rental unit and one for personal use at another address. A single supplier receipt needs delivery annotations before the study team can place either purchase in the property inventory.
question: Can I use the platform payout statement as the property asset record?
answer: No. It can help establish activity dates, but it does not describe acquisition costs, equipment ownership, or what each contractor installed.

angle: Check residential use before underwriting an accessory rental
local: Clearwater’s ADU guidance states that short-term rentals are not permitted in residential zoning districts. Verify the address-specific use before treating a residential guest-unit project as a nightly rental investment.
scope: If the intended operation changes to a longer lease, the construction records remain useful, but the study scope and owner’s tax assumptions need review. Identify the original dwelling, the accessory addition, and shared utility upgrades. Avoid combining an unapproved rental projection with an assumed accelerated deduction in the investment budget.
records: Written zoning/use confirmation for the parcel
ADU construction contract and shared-service breakdown
Actual leasing plan and readiness timeline
scenario: A homeowner builds an accessory suite expecting nightly bookings, then arranges a longer-term tenancy. Preserve the suite’s construction evidence and give the preparer the actual lease and use dates instead of the original vacation-rental projection.
question: Can cost segregation make an otherwise prohibited rental permissible?
answer: No. A study analyzes property costs. Resolve lawful operation independently and use the actual rental arrangement when evaluating tax treatment and the value of commissioning a report.

angle: Separate rehabilitation work from the purchase of an older rental
local: Cleveland’s rental-registration page discusses the Certificate Approving Rental Occupancy and a separate registration path for vacant property. Keep those status records alongside the rehabilitation timeline.
scope: For a vacant building prepared for guests or tenants, distinguish what was acquired from what the buyer removed, repaired, or installed. Inspection correction lists help locate work but do not show its final cost. Reconcile each contractor’s final invoice to the ledger, including credits for work deleted from the original scope.
records: Acquisition photographs and initial inspection findings
Rehabilitation contracts with credits and change orders
Occupancy records and dates completed spaces became available
scenario: A contractor quotes replacement of every kitchen cabinet but ultimately repairs some and replaces others. Give the provider the revised scope and final photographs. The first estimate would describe assets that were never installed.
question: Should I submit the renovation estimate or the final invoice?
answer: Submit the final reconciled costs, with the estimate and change history when they explain scope. Identify unpaid, disputed, or cancelled work instead of assuming the quoted amount became property basis.

angle: Verify the parcel behind a lake-access rental description
local: The Kootenai County Assessor offers parcel information and ownership mapping. Use the parcel identifier to connect a Coeur d’Alene property’s listing description with the real estate actually acquired.
scope: A purchase described as lake-access may include a residence, another tax parcel, an easement, or an association membership. Provide the deed package and settlement allocation for all interests. Have the preparer resolve land and non-building interests before the provider inventories improvements; a marketing premium is not an itemized asset cost.
records: Deeds and parcel numbers for every acquired interest
Access easements and association ownership documents
Settlement statement and supported land allocation
scenario: A buyer closes on a house and an adjoining vacant lot under one contract. The study should not treat the second parcel’s entire price as improvements merely because both parcels support the same guest listing.
question: Can the parcel record confirm rental permission?
answer: An assessor record is primarily a property identification and valuation resource. Confirm operating eligibility with the relevant planning authority and keep that answer separate from the ownership file.

angle: Keep the new owner’s approval and the seller’s property history separate
local: Colorado Springs states that an STR permit is issued to a specific owner rather than running with the property. Confirm your own operating status when acquiring an existing rental.
scope: A going-concern sale can include reservation history, furnishings, and recent seller improvements. For a property study, reconcile what the buyer acquired under the contract rather than simply importing the seller’s depreciation schedule. Preserve old records as descriptive evidence and clearly distinguish them from the buyer’s cost documentation.
records: Buyer closing statement and executed asset schedule
Seller inventory verified at possession
New owner’s permit file and post-closing improvement receipts
scenario: A seller supplies a depreciation report from an earlier acquisition. The buyer pays a different price and excludes several furniture items from the sale. Give the provider both the historical report and the current contract, with the excluded items identified.
question: Can I reuse the seller’s study without adjustment?
answer: Ask the provider and return preparer to evaluate it. The prior report may help describe components, but it does not establish your transaction costs or automatically become your depreciation schedule.

angle: Resolve the operating plan before valuing a furnished conversion
local: Dallas publishes STR registration provisions in its code. Because published code alone may not describe current enforcement or litigation effects, confirm the property’s current operating status directly before relying on a short-stay projection.
scope: A furnished townhome may alternate between corporate leases and shorter stays. Keep the actual contracts and use calendar, and disclose any change in the intended operation. Study costs should be tied to property evidence, while the return preparer separately evaluates the rental activity and whether projected deductions can be used.
records: Actual leases and booking durations
Written operating-status confirmation
Furnishing invoices separated from leasing and marketing costs
scenario: An investor furnishes a unit for visiting professionals but later uses six-month leases. The same furniture remains on site, yet the operating facts differ from the original proposal. Update the provider and preparer before treating a preliminary STR tax illustration as applicable.
question: Does a short-term-rental label determine passive-activity treatment?
answer: No. Supply the real rental periods, services, participation, and ownership facts to the preparer. A city category or marketing label does not resolve federal tax treatment.

angle: Describe lake-house amenities by ownership and installation
source_label: Garrett County transient vacation rental units
local: Garrett County publishes information for transient vacation rental units. Match the county operating file to the Deep Creek parcel and the specific structures included in the rental.
scope: A lake house can include an indoor pool enclosure, mechanical equipment, a detached garage, and outdoor recreation areas. Ask contractors to distinguish equipment from the structure housing it and from general building systems. Show the provider how each element functions instead of applying one classification to the entire amenity package.
records: Building plans identifying the pool enclosure and mechanical room
Equipment model numbers and installation invoices
Separate schedules for residence, garage, and exterior work
scenario: A pool project invoice combines the enclosure, circulation equipment, dehumidification, and furnishings. Request a scope breakdown with installation locations. The term indoor pool does not establish a single cost or classification for those different components.
question: Will every guest amenity qualify for the same recovery period?
answer: No. The provider must analyze the asset and its function. Give the preparer component evidence rather than assuming a classification from the amenity’s appeal to guests.

angle: Keep cottage operating permits and furniture transfers traceable
source_label: Door County Tourism Zone lodging permits
local: The Door County Tourism Zone Commission provides a lodging-permit application for property owners. Confirm the municipality and other applicable approvals as well as the tourism-zone account.
scope: For a small group of seasonal cottages, maintain an inventory for each cottage even when one manager purchases supplies. Furniture moved between buildings should have a transfer record rather than a second acquisition entry. Distinguish shared storage, grounds equipment, and guest furnishings when defining the study engagement.
records: Cottage-by-cottage ownership and permit schedule
Furniture purchase and inter-cottage transfer log
Shared maintenance-equipment records and storage location
scenario: A manager moves dining furniture from Cottage A to Cottage B and replaces it in A. The transfer is not a new purchase for B. Keep the original asset identifier and new invoice so the two inventories reconcile to the total property records.
question: Can one manager’s annual spending report support the entire study?
answer: It is a starting point. Request underlying invoices and destinations so the provider can separate acquisitions, transfers, operating supplies, and work on common areas.

angle: Separate city-limit questions from a multi-building guest property
local: Fredericksburg’s permit FAQ distinguishes city limits from its extra-territorial jurisdiction. Establish the parcel’s location before assuming the same permit process applies to every property with a Fredericksburg address.
scope: A guest compound may contain an older residence, a later cottage, outdoor gathering space, and owner storage. Inventory each building by age, function, and cost source. Construction of a second guest unit should not overwrite the original home’s acquisition history or create a second entry for common utility work.
records: Parcel location and labeled compound plan
Separate acquisition and cottage-construction records
Shared utility and outdoor-area invoice detail
scenario: An owner adds a guest cottage beside an existing rental. The cottage contract includes a new water line that also serves the original house. Identify both connections and the incremental construction scope for the provider’s allocation review.
question: Does each guest building need an identical asset allocation?
answer: No. Building age, construction, furnishings, and ownership can differ. Ask for a property-specific analysis using each structure’s evidence rather than copying a percentage across the compound.

angle: Reconcile a guest-room setup with the zoning-clearance file
source_label: Fresno business tax and STR permit information
local: Fresno’s Finance Department provides STR permit information and applications. Its application materials direct owners to obtain zone clearance; retain that property-specific file when planning the operation.
scope: If only part of a residence is rented, identify dedicated guest furnishings and shared household equipment. Mark personal purchases and items brought into rental use later. A whole-house retail estimate is a poor substitute for a documented inventory of the actual rented rooms.
records: Zone-clearance and permit records for the address
Guest-room layout and shared-space description
Receipts identifying newly acquired and transferred furnishings
scenario: A host installs a guest-room mini refrigerator and also replaces the main kitchen refrigerator. Note whether the main kitchen remains shared with the owner. The two appliances should not be described as serving identical rental space without supporting facts.
question: Can I claim the whole furnishing package if I rent one bedroom?
answer: Have the preparer determine the appropriate treatment from actual use. Supply room measurements, access arrangements, and costs rather than applying a whole-property estimate to a partial rental.

angle: Reconcile ownership changes with city registration and elevated-home work
local: Galveston’s FAQ explains the city-administered registration process following the transfer from the Park Board. Use the current property identifier and preserve earlier records when ownership or management changes.
scope: For an elevated coastal home, describe the stairs, platforms, enclosed areas, and equipment separately. Contractor invoices often combine access work with storm repairs or replacements. Show which components existed at purchase and which were installed later, and provide insurance or reimbursement information to the return preparer when relevant.
records: Closing photographs of elevated and ground-level areas
Access-structure and equipment repair invoices
Insurance settlement documents separated from construction cost detail
