scenario: A buyer replaces damaged stairs and adds a new outdoor rinse station after closing. An invoice titled exterior repairs hides two different scopes. Ask for a breakdown and retain dated photos so the provider can identify the acquired and newly constructed elements.
question: Can I use an insurance estimate as the final project cost?
answer: It may help describe damage, but reconcile actual work, invoices, reimbursements, and payments with the preparer. Estimated replacement work may differ from what was completed.

angle: Separate driveway changes from rental furnishings and resort access
source_label: Hilton Head Island town update, June 20, 2026
local: The town’s June 2026 update discusses the revised STR ordinance and restrictions on expanding parking for rental guests. Check the current requirements before including proposed site changes in a property plan.
scope: A villa or home may have association-controlled roads and recreation facilities alongside owner-funded parking or interior work. Identify who owns and pays for each improvement. Proposed construction should remain outside completed-cost schedules until the facts and costs are resolved; the provider needs the property as acquired and actually improved.
records: Association declaration and exterior-work approvals
Completed parking or landscaping invoices
Villa inventory and manager-provided replacement records
scenario: An owner budgets a driveway expansion but instead purchases indoor storage after a permitting review. Give the provider the completed storage invoice and remove the unbuilt driveway from the project ledger. A budget line is not evidence of an installed improvement.
question: Does an association assessment identify an asset automatically?
answer: No. Obtain the purpose, underlying project detail, and ownership terms. The preparer must distinguish the payment from the particular property interest or work it supports.

angle: Build a cost map for cabins sharing land and utilities
local: Hocking County provides lodging-tax information for local STR operators, including county and township requirements. Identify the township and parcel for each cabin rather than treating Hocking Hills as one jurisdiction.
scope: When several cabins share a well, septic system, access road, or maintenance building, prepare a site map with connections and construction dates. Trace shared invoices once and give the provider a documented allocation question. A per-cabin estimate should not multiply the same infrastructure cost by the number of listings.
records: Parcel and township schedule for each cabin
Utility and access-road plans with contractor invoices
Cabin-specific furnishing lists and opening dates
scenario: Three cabins are completed in stages using one well. The initial construction ledger places the well in the first phase, while later proposals repeat a standard utility allowance. Reconcile the actual shared system before combining those phase budgets.
question: Can separate booking listings be treated as separate complete properties?
answer: Not without checking shared ownership and improvements. Define the reporting units and shared costs before the study so the total agrees with the owner’s records.

angle: Match the tax map key to the unit’s ownership and rental authorization
source_label: Honolulu Planning and Permitting STR FAQ
local: Honolulu’s Planning and Permitting FAQ discusses STR registration or nonconforming-use identifiers and the tax map key used in advertising. Confirm the current status of the actual unit rather than relying on a neighboring rental.
scope: For a condominium purchase, reconcile the unit description, deed, furnishings, and any separate parking or storage interest. A unit’s guest access to hotel-style services does not establish ownership of the building’s equipment. Give the preparer leasehold or other title terms when those apply.
records: Tax map key and unit-specific title documents
Rental authorization records and operating timeline
Furniture package, parking, and storage acquisition detail
scenario: A buyer acquires a furnished unit with an assigned parking right. The sales brochure also advertises a pool and lobby. Separate the deeded or contractual interests from shared amenities before asking the provider to allocate the purchase price.
question: Can the building’s rental reputation establish my unit’s status?
answer: No. Confirm unit-specific permission with the authority and ownership with the documents. Neither the building name nor a seller’s advertised return supplies those answers.

angle: Distinguish a hosted homeshare from a whole-home operating history
local: Hood River’s planning page distinguishes hosted homeshares and vacation home rentals and describes annual licensing. Use the category applicable to the property’s actual arrangement when assembling operating records.
scope: A home that shifts from hosted rooms to another rental arrangement needs a clear use timeline. Identify furnishings retained through the change, additions purchased later, and spaces that remain personal. Ask the preparer to resolve allocation before the provider extrapolates component costs across all square footage.
records: License category and dated use changes
Room measurements and access descriptions
Inventory showing retained furnishings and new acquisitions
scenario: A host first rents a basement room and later moves out while keeping an upstairs room locked for personal storage. The guest listing may describe a whole home, but the study file should show the excluded room and how shared systems serve the building.
question: Does whole-home advertising mean every room is in rental use?
answer: No. Document actual access and use. Listing language can differ from the physical arrangement, especially where owners retain storage or private rooms.

angle: Keep registration identifiers consistent across a townhome portfolio
local: Houston’s Administration and Regulatory Affairs page explains STR registration and the city-issued identifier used in listings. Match that identifier with the legal address in each property’s study file.
scope: A townhome portfolio often contains similar floor plans purchased at different times and prices. Give each property its own closing reconciliation and improvement history. Similar construction may help organize an inspection, but it does not justify copying the same dollar allocation or furnishing inventory across every address.
records: Address-to-registration crosswalk
Separate closing statements and land allocations
Townhome-specific inventory and later improvement ledger
scenario: Two neighboring units have identical layouts, but one was acquired furnished and the other was furnished by the owner. Separate seller-acquired items from retail purchases and record the different costs; a shared floor plan does not make those transactions equivalent.
question: Can the provider inspect one unit and assume all others are identical?
answer: Ask how differences will be verified and documented. Disclose remodels, finish variations, and furnishings so the engagement’s evidence plan fits the portfolio instead of relying on appearance alone.

angle: Reconcile event-rental preparation with continuing residential use
local: Indianapolis publishes documents addressing its short-term rental permit program. Check current administration and address-specific requirements with the city before relying on an occasional event-rental plan.
scope: A home prepared for a few high-demand weekends can remain substantially personal property. Document the actual guest dates, owner occupancy, and equipment use before requesting a savings estimate. Improvements to the entire residence and temporary guest supplies should be distinguishable in the records given to the return preparer.
records: Event and ordinary-use calendar
Inventory distinguishing household items from guest-only purchases
Improvement invoices with locations and purposes
scenario: An owner buys extra beds and rents the home during an event, then returns the rooms to family use. Provide the actual dates and subsequent use. A gross booking receipt does not establish that the whole residence became a year-round rental.
question: Is a study worthwhile for a handful of rental dates?
answer: Have the preparer evaluate the use pattern, applicable limitations, and expected benefit against the fee first. Limited rental activity can materially change the economics of commissioning a study.

angle: Distinguish boat access and marine equipment from the dwelling
local: Islamorada publishes vacation-rental licensing and annual-registration information. Confirm the status of the specific unit and retain the operating file independently of the property-cost analysis.
scope: A waterfront rental may advertise a dock, lift, fish-cleaning station, or marina access. Establish whether each feature is owned, leased, shared, or excluded from the transaction. Identify construction materials, installation, and utility connections; a broad marine-amenity allowance cannot describe those differences.
records: Title and dock or marina agreements
Lift and dock invoices with installation scope
Purchase inventory identifying included and excluded equipment
scenario: A home sale includes a privately owned boat lift but only a membership right to another marina facility. Record the different legal interests and provide the acquisition documents. Guest use of both facilities does not mean the owner acquired comparable physical assets.
question: Does waterfront access make all related costs building improvements?
answer: No. Ask the provider and preparer to evaluate ownership, function, and supporting costs. Water access is a marketing description, not a classification method.

angle: Distinguish Jackson’s lodging overlay from the broader destination
local: The Town of Jackson explains different STR procedures inside and outside its lodging overlay. A Jackson Hole market description can include property beyond town boundaries, so identify the parcel and authority first.
scope: A mountain residence used part-time by its owner needs records of owner stays, guest stays, and improvements made between seasons. If a manager controls reservations and maintenance, obtain detailed exports rather than only annual net income. That timeline helps the preparer evaluate use and the provider distinguish acquired assets from subsequent work.
records: Parcel location and applicable operating approval
Manager calendar including owner blocks
Seasonal work orders with invoices and completion dates
scenario: A manager blocks several weeks for a kitchen project and separately blocks an owner holiday. Label those periods accurately; treating both as generic unavailable dates hides facts needed for the use analysis.
question: Can the manager’s occupancy percentage establish the tax allocation?
answer: Not by itself. Ask for the underlying dates and reasons for blocked periods. Marketing occupancy metrics may exclude owner time or maintenance in ways that do not answer tax questions.

angle: Reconcile multiple parcels and improvements against Duval records
local: The Duval County Property Appraiser provides real-estate and tangible-property searches. Use the records to identify the parcels and property descriptions associated with the rental acquisition.
scope: A rental house and a separate garage parcel can be sold together, while the closing statement reports a single price. Give the preparer every deed and the available valuation support. The provider should know which parcel holds each improvement and whether the buyer later added or removed equipment.
records: All deed and parcel references from the closing
Survey locating the residence and detached improvements
Purchase allocation and post-closing additions
scenario: A buyer receives a residence and an adjacent parcel containing a workshop. Only the residence is furnished for guests. Explain the workshop’s actual use and ownership rather than treating the whole combined price as the guest dwelling.
question: Can property-search values be copied into the study as purchase costs?
answer: Use them as contextual records, not an automatic substitute for the acquisition reconciliation. The preparer must determine the appropriate basis using the transaction and applicable tax rules.

angle: Separate occasional event use from a continuing rental business
local: Kansas City’s STR program provides registration information and a list of registered properties. Confirm the applicable registration category and operating period for the specific Missouri address.
scope: An event-focused rental can have a very different use pattern from a continuously available investment property. Record when the home was available, rented, and personally occupied. Keep temporary staging, rented equipment, and acquired furnishings separate so the preparer can assess the facts before a component study is proposed.
records: Registration category and actual operating dates
Staging rental agreements versus purchase receipts
Owner-use calendar and property readiness records
scenario: A household rents extra televisions for an event weekend and buys new mattresses it keeps afterward. The rented equipment is not an owned asset for a property inventory. Identify the contracts and what remained after the guests left.
question: Will event revenue alone make a study economically attractive?
answer: No. Compare the study fee and expected usable tax benefit using the actual ownership and use facts. High nightly revenue does not establish a large depreciable acquisition or an immediately usable deduction.

angle: Keep a transient license transaction separate from physical property costs
local: Key West describes transient rental medallions among its regulatory licenses. Confirm the unit’s current authorization and any transfer requirements through the city rather than assuming a sale transfers every operating right.
scope: When a transaction separately values a license or other operating interest, flag it for the preparer. A cost segregation study of physical components should not silently treat that value as furniture or building improvements. Include the contract allocation and any separate transfer documents in the engagement file.
records: Purchase agreement and asset allocation exhibits
Transient-license records and transfer documents
Physical inventory verified at closing
scenario: A contract lists real estate, furnishings, and a separately negotiated operating right. Present all three lines to the preparer. Combining them into one building-cost figure would conceal a classification question that should be resolved before the study.
question: Can the study provider allocate every part of a going-concern price?
answer: Clarify the engagement scope. Physical component analysis may not cover intangible rights or other transaction interests; the return preparer should coordinate those allocations.

angle: Identify the rental category and the actual seasonal improvement scope
local: Lake Geneva’s city page describes rental categories and provides a registration portal. Establish whether the property falls within the city and which category matches the operation.
scope: A lake-area home may open seasonally and undergo exterior work during the off-season. Record completion and readiness dates for each project, especially if the dwelling remains available while a detached feature is unfinished. The booking calendar alone does not describe when every addition was installed.
records: City category and rental calendar
Exterior project schedule with completion evidence
Separate dwelling and detached-amenity cost records
scenario: An owner finishes interior furnishing in spring but installs an outdoor kitchen later. Keep the later installation and utility work out of the original furnishing package, and explain when each area became ready for its intended use.
question: Do all improvements take the first guest’s arrival date?
answer: Not necessarily. Provide the preparer with each project’s completion and availability evidence. A single first-booking date may not describe additions completed months later.

angle: Confirm city boundaries before preparing a home-sharing study
source_label: City of Las Vegas STR resources
local: The City of Las Vegas provides license and location resources for short-term rentals. A Las Vegas mailing address does not by itself establish that city rules govern the property; confirm the actual jurisdiction.
scope: For an owner-occupied arrangement, distinguish guest rooms from the owner’s rooms and shared entertainment areas. Identify whether pool equipment, security systems, and kitchen purchases serve the entire residence. A listing’s amenity count should not be converted into a full-property asset allocation without use evidence.
records: Jurisdiction confirmation and operating approval
Guest and owner room map
Amenity invoices with locations and shared-use notes
scenario: A host installs smart locks on guest rooms and a security system covering the whole property. Document those different functions. A combined technology receipt does not demonstrate that every item serves the same rented area.
question: Can a nearby licensed rental establish eligibility for my address?
answer: No. Check your own parcel, ownership, and operating facts. The provider’s property analysis also requires your records rather than another home’s component percentages.

angle: Separate city zoning from a cabin marketed to Leavenworth visitors
source_label: Leavenworth zoning maps and planning regulations
local: Leavenworth’s Community Development resources include zoning and area maps. Use them to establish the city boundary; a cabin marketed to the Leavenworth destination may require a county inquiry instead.
scope: For a cabin with a detached sauna or recreation shelter, show the structures and their utility connections on a simple site plan. Separate the purchased equipment from the enclosure and installation work. The provider needs to know whether a feature is movable equipment, part of a structure, or a shared system before evaluating classification.
records: Parcel map and jurisdiction record
Sauna equipment invoice and enclosure construction scope
Site electrical and water-service descriptions
scenario: A contractor quotes a complete sauna package that includes the unit, platform, shelter, and electrical extension. Request an itemized final statement. A single amenity name does not explain the underlying assets or the portion serving other buildings.
question: Does a detached structure automatically receive a short recovery period?
answer: No. Its construction and function matter. Supply drawings and installation details and let the provider support the classification rather than assuming detachment determines tax treatment.

angle: Build the study around actual home-sharing rooms and dates
local: Los Angeles City Planning provides a home-sharing records portal and renewal resources. Match the registered property and permitted operation with the rooms and dates in your own records.
scope: A host may rent a bedroom, the main living area during travel, or different areas at different times. Record those changes instead of using one annual whole-house percentage without explanation. Separate personal décor from guest-only furnishings and identify any improvements made before the home-sharing activity began.
records: Home-sharing registration and room-use history
Owner travel and guest booking calendar
Furnishing receipts labeled by room and actual use
scenario: A resident rents a spare room most months and the whole dwelling while traveling. A sofa serves the household throughout the year while a new bed serves the rented room. Present those differences to the preparer before applying any rental allocation.
question: Does a home-sharing registration make the entire residence depreciable?
answer: No. The preparer must evaluate actual rental and personal use. Registration is operating documentation, not a determination of the eligible basis or deduction.

angle: Distinguish a main dwelling from a separately improved carriage space
local: Louisville Metro’s planning resources address STR registration and conditional-use processes. Confirm the approval applicable to the actual dwelling and retain supporting residence documentation when relevant.
scope: A carriage-house or rear-unit project may combine preexisting structure, new living-space construction, and furnishings. Identify the areas changed and reconcile contractor work to the original acquisition. If the main house remains personally occupied, show which access and utility improvements serve both spaces.
records: Main-house and rear-unit plans
Conversion invoices separating shell, systems, and furnishings
Shared access and utility-cost descriptions
scenario: An owner finishes a garage loft for guests while retaining the lower garage for personal storage. Supply section drawings or photographs showing the two uses. Applying the loft’s rental description to the entire garage could misstate the study scope.
question: Is a separate listing enough to separate a rear unit’s costs?
answer: No. Provide physical measurements, construction records, and shared-system details. The provider and preparer need a supported allocation, not simply separate marketing names.

angle: Capture delivery and installation costs in a seasonal furnishing project
source_label: Mackinac Island city permits and license documents
local: Mackinac Island’s city document library includes permits, license applications, and planning materials. Identify the applicable operating and construction records for the property before organizing the study file.
scope: A seasonal lodging refurbishment can generate separate bills for goods, freight, handling, storage, and installation. Tie those bills to the assets delivered rather than keeping an unexplained logistics total. Identify items never installed, damaged in transit, or returned before reopening and reconcile credits with the purchasing ledger.
records: Vendor invoices and delivery manifests
Freight, storage, and installation charges tied to purchases
Returned-item credits and final room inventory
scenario: A furnishings order arrives in several shipments, and damaged chairs are replaced under a vendor credit. Reconcile quantities received and the credit before allocating related freight. Counting every shipment as a new acquisition would overstate the installed inventory.
question: Can transportation charges be left outside the study records?
answer: Give them to the preparer with the related purchase documents. Their treatment depends on the facts; omitting them or allocating them twice can distort the cost reconciliation.

angle: Connect the certified unit to manager-controlled refurbishment records
source_label: Mammoth Lakes transient rental and certification information
local: Mammoth Lakes provides information about Certified Property Authorization and business-tax administration. Keep the unit’s authorization separate from the manager’s business account when assembling ownership records.
scope: A manager may pay for furniture replacements, deduct maintenance charges, and retain reserve funds before remitting income. Request the underlying invoices and authorization trail. Net remittances cannot show which assets the owner acquired, whether an item was repaired, or whether a charge was merely held for future work.
records: Unit authorization and management agreement
Reserve activity reconciled to paid vendor invoices
Refurbishment inventory and dated installation photos
scenario: A manager withholds a refurbishment reserve in one year but completes the furniture purchase in another. Preserve both the reserve ledger and purchase documentation. The withholding date alone does not establish when an asset was acquired or ready for use.
question: Is the manager’s annual expense summary enough for a component study?
answer: Usually more detail is needed. Request descriptions, vendor documents, credits, and installed locations so the provider can distinguish property work from operating charges.

angle: Keep city records separate from the county vacation-rental program
local: Collier County’s registration page expressly excludes properties within Marco Island from that county ordinance. Check the applicable city process instead of assuming a county registration establishes the unit’s status.
scope: For a condominium renovation, separate the owner’s interior project from association work on roofs, façades, and shared mechanical systems. Obtain assessment notices and supporting project descriptions. Ask the preparer to determine the treatment of association payments before the provider lists them as owner-installed components.
records: Condominium declaration and owner responsibility schedule
Interior contractor invoices and appliance inventory
Assessment notices with association project detail
scenario: An owner pays a building-wide exterior assessment while replacing cabinets inside the unit. The payments have different ownership and scope evidence. Give the provider both files rather than combining them under a general renovation allowance.
question: Does paying an assessment establish direct ownership of the completed work?
answer: Not by itself. The governing documents and project arrangement matter. The preparer should resolve the owner’s interest and treatment using the underlying records.

angle: Reconcile an older rental’s prior schedule before furnishing it for guests
local: Memphis’s licenses page directs STR operators to the registry maintained by the Memphis and Shelby County planning department. Align the registered address with the ownership and prior rental records.
scope: If a previously unfurnished rental becomes a furnished guest property, distinguish the old building schedule from new acquisitions. Record removed fixtures and any replaced equipment instead of leaving both old and new items unexplained. The return preparer needs the prior schedule to coordinate implementation of a new study.
records: Prior depreciation schedule and acquisition documents
Turnover inventory of retained and removed items
New furnishing and replacement-equipment invoices
scenario: A landlord replaces old appliances before switching to short stays. The accountant’s schedule still includes the previous appliance entries. Provide the removal date and new receipts so the preparer can reconcile the old records with the proposed study.
question: Can a new report simply replace the old depreciation spreadsheet?
answer: The preparer should reconcile the schedules and determine the implementation method. Preserve the historical file; unexplained replacement can lose accumulated depreciation and asset-history information.

angle: Separate pool systems from outdoor entertainment purchases
local: Mesa’s licensing resource describes the local STR license and its relationship to Arizona transaction privilege tax documentation. Keep the city record and property identifier consistent with the study file.
scope: An outdoor renovation may combine pool pumps, resurfacing, shade structures, movable seating, and lighting. Request descriptions of what each system serves and whether equipment is independently identifiable. A single backyard entertainment label does not support one classification for the entire project.
records: Pool-system specifications and equipment receipts
Shade and lighting plans with installation locations
Outdoor furniture inventory and project invoice reconciliation
scenario: A pool contractor replaces the pump and resurfaces the basin, while another supplier delivers loungers. Keep the scopes separate, including labor and credits. The provider can then analyze the actual components rather than a blended backyard estimate.
question: Will every outdoor item receive the same depreciation treatment?
answer: No. Ownership, physical function, and installation matter. Ask for supported component conclusions and have the return preparer evaluate how the report applies to the owner.

angle: Confirm lodging use before analyzing a residential conversion
source_label: City of Miami STR and lodging conversion procedures
local: The City of Miami publishes procedures for converting property to lodging and identifies zoning restrictions. Distinguish the city from Miami Beach or unincorporated Miami-Dade; their operating processes are not interchangeable.
scope: A conversion budget can contain permitting, architectural work, life-safety improvements, room buildouts, and furniture. Separate completed work from proposals and abandoned options. The study provider needs the actual physical scope, while the preparer addresses the treatment of costs that are not simply installed building components.
records: Address-specific zoning and occupancy documents
Final conversion cost ledger by scope
Furniture acquisition records and abandoned-project costs separately identified
scenario: An investor plans a lodging conversion but revises the project to conventional leases after a zoning review. Give the provider the completed plans and actual operation, not the earlier hotel-style furniture budget.
question: Can a city lodging designation determine a federal recovery period?
answer: No. The return preparer must evaluate the property’s facts under applicable tax rules. Local land-use terminology and federal depreciation categories serve different purposes.

angle: Use inspection corrections to locate costs, not to classify them
local: Milwaukee’s Department of Neighborhood Services administers tourist-rooming-house licensing and inspections. Save the relevant checklist and correction notices with the property’s operating records.
scope: Before a furnished rental opens, inspection work may include alarms, handrails, electrical corrections, or changes to guest facilities. Match each correction to the final invoice and identify what was actually installed. The inspection category does not itself determine whether a cost is a repair, equipment, or a building component.
records: Inspection checklist with resolved correction items
Final contractor invoices tied to each correction
Opening inventory and photographs of completed work
scenario: An electrician’s invoice combines correction of existing wiring and installation of new guest-room equipment. Ask for the scope and locations of each task. One inspection sign-off cannot explain the cost and function of both.
question: Does passing inspection prove that a study is complete?
answer: No. Inspection addresses operating standards. A study still needs ownership, acquisition-cost reconciliation, component evidence, and a clear handoff to the return preparer.

angle: Identify the actual hosting unit within a mixed-use duplex
local: Minneapolis provides a short-term rental hosting-license resource for properties offered through booking platforms. Match the hosting unit to the building’s legal address and physical layout.
scope: If one unit is owner occupied and another hosts visitors, identify shared heating, laundry, and circulation areas. Separate unit-specific furnishings from building-wide improvements. Explain ownership and use of detached storage or garages rather than assuming the hosting unit includes the entire parcel.
records: Unit layout with owner and guest areas labeled
Shared-system invoices and areas served
Guest-unit purchase inventory and exclusive-use notes
scenario: A duplex owner buys a new furnace serving both units and installs a dishwasher only in the guest unit. Record the different service areas. Applying the guest-unit allocation identically to both purchases would conceal material facts.
question: Can the registered unit number replace a floor plan?
answer: No. The identifier helps match records, but measurements and use descriptions show which assets and spaces the study should address.

angle: Verify the approved lodging footprint before studying an expansion
local: Moab’s Planning and Zoning Department administers the city’s land-use rules. Confirm the approved use and footprint directly for a lodging property, including whether the parcel lies in the city or surrounding county.
scope: For an existing guest property, distinguish approved rooms and completed improvements from a proposed expansion. Keep separate records for equipment serving the current operation and infrastructure installed for later phases. Do not include a conceptual additional unit as though it were an acquired or completed asset.
records: Approved site plan and written use confirmation
Existing-building inventory and acquisition records
Expansion design, budget, and completed costs separately tracked
scenario: An owner buys an operating rental and plans a second guest building. Only a utility trench is completed before the project pauses. Tell the provider exactly what exists, what it serves, and what remains proposed rather than submitting the full expansion budget.
question: Can a seller’s description establish expansion rights?
answer: No. Confirm current permission with the relevant authority. The study should describe the property actually acquired and improved, with unfinished or uncertain costs clearly identified for the preparer.

angle: Separate a resort unit’s interior from the building’s lodging operation
source_label: Myrtle Beach published zoning overlay provisions
local: Myrtle Beach publishes zoning overlay provisions that include rental-use considerations. Confirm the specific unit’s permitted operation and jurisdiction rather than treating all properties advertised to beach visitors alike.
scope: A resort unit may participate in a rental pool while the operator controls common facilities and periodic furnishing replacements. Obtain the unit ownership documents and itemized replacement statements. Guest access to pools, corridors, or front-desk services does not mean those facilities should appear as separately owned unit assets.
records: Unit deed and rental-pool agreement
Operator furnishing purchases and reserve accounting
Owner-funded interior renovation scope
scenario: A rental-pool statement deducts a furniture reserve and a common-area maintenance fee. Request the underlying documents before treating either line as an acquisition. One may fund future work and the other may cover operations rather than installed unit property.
question: Is rental-pool income enough to value the furnishings?
answer: No. Income reports describe performance. The study needs purchase and ownership evidence for the actual property interests, including what the operator rather than the owner provides.

angle: Align the permitted unit with the historic building’s physical scope
source_label: New Orleans published STR zoning provisions
local: New Orleans publishes STR provisions through its Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Confirm current permit status for the actual unit; published provisions and a property’s past rental history do not by themselves establish present authorization.
scope: For an older house divided into multiple units, describe shared porches, stairs, and systems separately from each unit’s interior. Keep preservation or repair work tied to detailed contractor descriptions. Architectural character does not tell the provider how a particular component functions or what the owner paid.
records: Unit plan and current operating-status records
Acquisition photographs and restoration scopes
Shared-system costs separated from unit furnishings
scenario: A renovation restores a common porch and adds guest-room appliances inside one unit. The work occurs under one general contract but serves different areas. Request invoice detail so the study can distinguish shared construction from unit-specific assets.
question: Does historic character create an automatic cost segregation percentage?
answer: No. The provider should analyze documented components and ownership. Any separate historic-property tax issues require their own review by the preparer.

angle: Reconcile state registration with a seasonal owner-use calendar
local: Rhode Island’s Department of Business Regulation provides STR registration for properties listed through third-party hosting platforms. Confirm Newport’s separate local requirements and keep the property’s municipal records as well.
scope: An owner-used coastal residence may have short rental seasons and substantial personal occupancy. Preserve the actual dates and identify spaces withheld from guests. For renovations, distinguish ordinary household choices from improvements and equipment used in the rented areas; let the preparer evaluate the allocation before estimating benefits.
records: State and local registration records
Guest, owner, and maintenance calendar
Room-level furnishing and renovation invoices
scenario: A residence is rented for a summer period, while the owner retains a locked study and uses the house during the rest of the year. Show that room and the calendar explicitly. A listing described as an entire home may not reflect every use restriction.
question: Does registering on a state portal establish year-round business use?
answer: No. Registration and actual use are different evidence. The preparer needs the occupancy facts to evaluate the tax treatment and whether a study’s expected benefit supports its cost.

angle: Reconcile a finished basement with the existing building record
source_label: Omaha building, development, and rental-registration resources
local: Omaha’s Planning Department lists rental-registration and building services within its Building and Development Division. Use the applicable property records to document the approved configuration before preparing a study scope.
scope: A basement guest-space project can involve new rooms, egress work, shared mechanical systems, and movable furnishings. Give the provider before-and-after plans and final contractor detail. Distinguish the acquired shell from the later buildout, and explain which parts remain personal storage or serve the whole house.
records: Existing and completed basement plans
Egress, plumbing, and mechanical invoices by scope
Guest-space inventory and retained personal-storage areas
scenario: An owner finishes two rooms but leaves the mechanical and storage areas unchanged. A contractor’s total basement square footage includes all four areas. Mark the work boundaries so the provider does not treat untouched space as newly constructed guest accommodation.
question: Can finished square footage alone support the project allocation?
answer: It helps describe scale, but costs, function, and actual work boundaries are also needed. Supply the construction details instead of relying only on a cost-per-square-foot estimate.

angle: Separate the city property file from beach-area marketing
local: Pensacola’s Inspection Services portal provides access to city property and permitting services. Establish whether the rental is in the city or another jurisdiction before selecting inspection records for a beach-area property.
scope: After repairs or a change of ownership, reconcile the original acquisition, removed items, and completed replacements. Give the preparer insurance and reimbursement documents separately from contractor costs. A study of the remaining property needs an accurate current inventory as well as the history explaining how it changed.
records: Jurisdiction and permit references
Acquisition inventory with removed assets marked
Final repair invoices and reimbursement records
scenario: A furnished home is purchased and later receives replacement flooring after water damage. The owner’s inventory still describes the acquired flooring. Show the affected rooms and replacement date so the provider and preparer can coordinate the old and new records.
question: Should damaged items stay in the current inventory?
answer: Identify whether they remain, were repaired, or were removed. Preserve historical records, but do not present disposed items as still installed without explanation.

angle: Distinguish the licensed operator from the owner of improvements
local: Philadelphia’s limited-lodging resource explains the operator-license process and related business licensing. The operating entity named in a license should be reconciled with the person or entity that owns the property costs.
scope: A tenant hosting guests may own furniture and pay for alterations without owning the building. Supply the lease, landlord approvals, reimbursement clauses, and actual invoices. Do not commission a whole-building allocation using the landlord’s purchase price for a tenant’s furnishing project.
records: Lease and written alteration approvals
Ownership and reimbursement terms for installed items
Tenant-paid furniture and improvement invoices
scenario: A tenant installs shelving and buys beds, while the landlord pays for a new heating system. Mark who paid, who owns each item, and what happens at lease termination. The hosting license does not settle those property interests.
question: Can an operator depreciate everything in the rented dwelling?
answer: Ownership, costs, lease terms, and tax rules must be evaluated. Ask the preparer to define the eligible cost pool before engaging a provider for component analysis.

angle: Document the function of shade, cooling, and guest equipment
local: Phoenix’s program explains its transition from registration to a permit process. Use current city records for the address and retain the operating documents with the property file.
scope: A rental upgrade may include a general cooling-system replacement, patio shade, outdoor fans, and dedicated guest equipment. Ask for invoices identifying the spaces and functions served. Climate-related usefulness does not establish a single tax classification for all of those purchases.
records: Cooling-system scope and equipment specifications
Patio shade and electrical installation detail
Guest-equipment receipts and installed-location photographs
scenario: An HVAC contractor replaces the main system and adds a separate unit serving a converted room. Request the equipment and labor breakdown, plus the room’s actual use. The provider needs those distinctions rather than one total described as air conditioning.
question: Are all cooling costs treated as short-life equipment?
answer: No automatic conclusion follows from the equipment name. The provider must evaluate function and installation, and the preparer applies the resulting analysis to the owner’s tax facts.

angle: Separate the cabin shell from themed entertainment installations
source_label: Pigeon Forge Building Department and overnight-rental design resources
local: Pigeon Forge’s Building Department provides overnight-rental design considerations alongside permitting and inspection resources. Identify the city boundary and retain the approved plans for the actual cabin.
scope: A themed rental can combine built-in bunk structures, movable arcade equipment, theater seating, decorative finishes, and ordinary building systems. Request a scope that distinguishes these items rather than assigning the entire entertainment buildout to furniture. Keep designs and photographs showing attachment and function.
records: Approved cabin plans and entertainment-room layout
Built-in construction invoices separate from purchased equipment
Delivery inventory and installation photographs
scenario: A cabin’s game-room invoice includes wall construction, specialty electrical work, and freestanding arcade machines. Ask the contractor and supplier for separate detail. A single entertainment package price does not explain which elements are part of the building.
question: Does calling a room a theater determine how its costs depreciate?
answer: No. Document the actual components, their use, and installation. The provider should support each classification instead of relying on the room’s marketing theme.

angle: Reconcile a converted house’s unit count and common systems
local: Pittsburgh describes its residential rental permit program through Permits, Licenses, and Inspections. Retain the applicable unit and building records, and separately confirm the permitted operating use for the property.
scope: An older house converted into several rentals may have shared stairs, one boiler, multiple kitchens, and later unit-by-unit renovations. Reconcile the physical unit count to the closing documents and prior asset schedule. Label which work serves one apartment and which supports the entire structure.
records: Current unit plan and acquisition description
Shared boiler and circulation-area invoices
Unit renovation dates and prior depreciation records
scenario: An owner updates one apartment for furnished stays while two other apartments retain annual tenants. The study should identify the new furniture and unit work without duplicating the building’s existing shared systems in all three units.
question: Does one parcel number mean the units have identical study facts?
answer: No. A parcel can contain different uses and improvement histories. Provide a unit schedule and explain shared components so the report reconciles to the whole property.

angle: Map the accessory rental area before allocating household improvements
local: Portland’s accessory short-term rental guidance distinguishes permit and conditional-use paths. Keep the approved arrangement and actual room use in the property file rather than relying only on a platform listing.
scope: For a basement suite or rented bedrooms, mark exclusive guest areas, shared laundry, access routes, and owner-only rooms. Give the preparer measurements and use dates. A whole-house project such as roof work cannot be described as serving only the rental suite simply because guests benefit from it.
records: Approved room layout and permit category
Measurements of guest, shared, and personal areas
Whole-house versus suite-specific improvement invoices
scenario: A homeowner replaces the roof and installs a compact kitchenette in the guest suite during the same month. Record separate scopes and service areas. The timing of payment does not make the two projects equivalent for allocation purposes.
question: Can I base the study only on the suite’s nightly rate?
answer: No. Rental pricing does not establish component cost or the rental share of household assets. Use construction, acquisition, and actual-use evidence.

angle: Track island rental equipment separately from the dwelling
local: Put-in-Bay Township provides zoning contacts and information for owners receiving STR correspondence. Confirm whether the property falls under the township or village before selecting the applicable operating file.
scope: A guest property may offer bicycles, carts, or other equipment alongside lodging. Identify whether equipment is owned, leased, separately rented, or provided by another business. Keep maintenance and operating charges distinct from acquisition records, and ask the preparer whether each activity belongs in the same reporting scope.
records: Jurisdiction confirmation and property approval records
Equipment ownership or lease agreements
Separate equipment inventory and dwelling improvement ledger
scenario: A lodging operator advertises guest transportation supplied by an outside vendor. The vendor’s equipment should not appear as owner-acquired property in the home’s component inventory. Document the service agreement and separately list equipment the owner actually purchased.
question: Does an advertised amenity belong in my study inventory?
answer: Only after verifying the relevant ownership and cost facts. Guest access alone does not establish that you acquired the equipment or can include its value in the property basis.

angle: Match the zoning permit to a newly created guest unit
local: Raleigh’s STR resource explains the zoning permit and use of its identifier in advertisements. Reconcile that identifier with the physical unit shown on plans and in the study engagement.
scope: A guest unit created within an existing property can have dedicated appliances but shared electrical, drainage, or access work. Record the incremental construction and identify what existed before conversion. Give the preparer the original acquisition and any earlier depreciation records so the new project does not replace the whole property history.
records: Zoning permit and guest-unit floor plan
Conversion contract with shared-service detail
Original acquisition file and new equipment invoices
scenario: A homeowner encloses a former recreation room as a guest suite and adds a kitchenette. The project includes work on a shared electrical panel. Identify the new room scope and the panel’s service area rather than treating the entire house as newly built rental space.
question: Is a conversion budget enough to order the final report?
answer: Use it for preliminary scoping, but supply final invoices, credits, and completion evidence for the finished analysis. Budgets can include work that changed or was never performed.

angle: Keep city permits and county rules from being mixed in one file
source_label: City of Sacramento short-term vacation rentals
local: The City of Sacramento provides its own STR permit and business-tax information. A property in unincorporated Sacramento County follows a different inquiry, so confirm jurisdiction before assembling operating records.
scope: For a residence rented during owner travel, preserve actual personal and guest dates and describe which rooms are accessible. If furnishings are upgraded for both household and guest use, label that shared purpose. Ask the preparer to assess the rental allocation before using a whole-property study estimate.
records: City or county jurisdiction confirmation
Owner-travel and guest-stay calendar
Room-access map and furnishing purchase history
scenario: An owner buys new living-room furniture and rents the home during several trips. The furniture continues in household use between bookings. Present that pattern rather than labeling the purchase exclusively as STR furniture because it appears in the listing.
question: Does a short-term permit determine the allowable annual deduction?
answer: No. The preparer evaluates actual use and applicable limitations. Local approval provides operating context but does not calculate federal depreciation.

angle: Verify zoning before treating a basement as nightly lodging
local: Salt Lake City’s Planning FAQ addresses short-term rentals and directs readers to zoning resources. Check the specific address and permitted use before assuming a basement apartment can operate as nightly lodging.
scope: If the unit ultimately serves longer-term tenants, document that actual arrangement. Separate basement construction, dedicated appliances, and work on shared building systems. The provider should receive the completed scope and actual use rather than a short-stay business plan that never went into operation.
records: Address-specific zoning response and unit plan
Executed lease or actual booking history
Basement construction and shared-mechanical invoices
scenario: An owner prepares a basement for guests but signs a residential lease after reviewing zoning. The appliances remain installed, while the operational assumptions change. Update the preparer before relying on any earlier nonpassive-loss or STR savings illustration.
question: Can a cost segregation proposal confirm that nightly rental is legal?
answer: No. Resolve land use with the appropriate authority. Then evaluate a study using the property’s actual ownership, costs, and rental activity.

angle: Distinguish guesthouse construction from a purchased furnished residence
local: San Antonio provides permit application, renewal, and cancellation services for STR operators. Match each permitted unit with the structure and ownership records used for the study.
scope: A detached guesthouse added after purchase needs its own construction reconciliation. Separate site connections and access work from the guesthouse shell and owner-supplied furnishings. Show whether the main residence remains personal, rented separately, or included in the same guest arrangement.
records: Main-house and guesthouse use plan
Guesthouse contract and owner-supplied item receipts
Site connection invoices and separate readiness dates
scenario: A construction contract includes a standard appliance allowance, but the owner supplies upgraded appliances directly. Obtain the builder’s credit and the actual purchase invoice so the same allowance is not retained in the shell cost and counted again as equipment.
question: Should a new guesthouse use the main house’s acquisition date?
answer: Provide separate acquisition and construction timelines. The preparer needs the facts for each addition rather than assigning the original closing date to later improvements.

angle: Separate operator furnishings from a building owned by someone else
source_label: San Francisco Office of Short-Term Rentals
local: San Francisco’s Office of Short-Term Rentals administers the city’s residential rental regulations. Verify the operator and dwelling records with that office and distinguish them from property ownership documents.
scope: A resident host may own the dwelling or occupy it under a lease. Before a study is scoped, establish which improvements and furnishings the host owns and whether any costs were reimbursed. Building-wide values cannot simply be assigned to a resident who only purchased room furnishings.
records: Deed or lease showing the host’s property interest
Landlord consent and reimbursement terms where applicable
Host-owned furnishing receipts and room-use records
scenario: A tenant buys beds and removable shelving while the building owner renovates the kitchen. The host’s inventory should distinguish those purchases from the landlord’s work. A shared mailing address does not establish a common owner of every asset.
question: Does business registration establish a depreciable interest in the building?
answer: No. Have the preparer evaluate ownership and the actual costs incurred. Registration supports operating compliance; it does not replace title or lease evidence.

angle: Reconcile lodging receipts with the property’s mixed-use history
local: San Jose’s Finance Department publishes lodging-tax forms and information. Use the records applicable to the activity, and separately confirm planning requirements for the dwelling and its rental arrangement.
scope: A guest suite can shift between visiting family, paying guests, and longer-term occupancy. Keep actual calendars and identify shared kitchens, laundry, and utilities. Tax remittance records may corroborate activity but do not explain the purchase cost or rental-use allocation of the underlying components.
records: Guest and personal-use calendar by room
Lodging records reconciled to booking history
Suite-specific purchases and shared-system invoices
scenario: An owner installs laundry equipment used by both the household and guests, while a separate guest-room refrigerator is restricted to visitors. Describe access and use for both. Reporting lodging receipts does not make their use patterns identical.
question: Can lodging-tax payments serve as the depreciation schedule?
answer: No. They concern operating receipts. The study and return preparation need separate evidence of ownership, acquisition costs, readiness, and actual use.

angle: Reconcile restoration costs and the unit’s permitted rental use
local: Sanibel publishes dwelling-rental provisions in its land-development code. Confirm the applicable unit classification and operating requirements rather than assuming every island residence has the same rental permissions.
scope: For a restored property, separate retained components, removed assets, replacement construction, and new furnishings. Provide insurance and reimbursement information to the preparer alongside the cost records. A restoration budget may describe a proposed replacement standard that differs from the final installed property.
records: Pre-work photographs and retained/removed asset list
Final restoration invoices with change orders
Insurance records and new furnishing inventory
scenario: A unit is restored using different flooring and cabinets from the insurer’s initial estimate. Give the provider the final specifications and actual invoices, with reimbursements separately identified. The estimate alone would describe the wrong completed components.
question: Can I study the restored unit without its earlier records?
answer: Collect as much history as possible and identify gaps. The preparer needs to coordinate prior basis, losses, reimbursements, and replacements; a current inventory cannot resolve all of those issues by itself.

angle: Keep the operator license separate from the building’s asset records
local: Seattle distinguishes the STR operator license from the business license tax certificate. Keep both applicable records linked to the correct property and unit rather than treating one account as an asset register.
scope: For a backyard cottage or attached apartment, document its ownership and construction independently from the main dwelling. Identify common access, utility connections, and equipment serving both. If the unit was previously leased long term, provide its existing depreciation history before adding new furnishings.
records: Unit address and license cross-reference
Cottage or apartment construction and utility records
Prior rental schedule plus new guest-furnishing receipts
scenario: A detached cottage already used as a rental is furnished for shorter stays. The owner buys beds and kitchenware but makes no new building acquisition. Distinguish those additions from the existing structure so the provider can coordinate with the prior schedule.
question: Does obtaining a new operator license restart the property’s basis?
answer: No automatic reset follows. Give the preparer the acquisition, construction, and prior-use history, then have the study’s scope reconciled to those records.

angle: Identify the county before grouping cabins under a regional name
local: Shenandoah County publishes STR permit application resources. The broader Shenandoah destination includes other jurisdictions; use this source only for the county it covers and verify the cabin’s actual parcel location.
scope: For a rural property with more than one cabin, identify the dwelling, barn or storage building, access improvements, and shared infrastructure. Explain which spaces guests use and which support maintenance or personal activities. The scenic acreage around a cabin should not be treated as depreciable construction merely because it is part of the guest experience.
records: County and parcel schedule with site plan
Cabin and outbuilding use descriptions
Shared infrastructure invoices and supported land allocation
scenario: A buyer acquires a cabin, a maintenance barn, and undeveloped acreage under one agreement. The listing emphasizes hiking access across the land. Separate the acquired interests and actual improvements before the provider estimates any component costs.
question: Can acreage advertised as an amenity enter the building allocation?
answer: Land and improvements require separate analysis. Give the preparer the transaction and valuation support rather than allocating the whole purchase price to structures because guests enjoy the property.

angle: Reconcile rental registration with a condo’s lock-off configuration
source_label: South Padre Island STR registration and tax portal
local: South Padre Island provides an STR registration and tax portal through its service provider. Keep the registered address and unit identifiers consistent with the condominium documents and booking records.
scope: A lock-off condominium can be advertised as one accommodation or as separate guest spaces. Identify the legal ownership interest, shared entry, connecting doors, and equipment assigned to each side. Multiple listings should not multiply the acquisition cost or create duplicate inventories of shared furniture.
records: Condominium deed and lock-off floor plan
Listing-to-unit identifier crosswalk
Furnishing inventory identifying shared and exclusive items
scenario: An owner lists a two-bedroom unit either whole or as two connected spaces. The same sofa appears in photographs for both listings. Record it once, with its physical location, rather than using listing exports as separate asset inventories.
question: Does each listing need a separate allocation of the full purchase price?
answer: No. Define the legal property and reporting scope first. The provider should reconcile any unit-level schedules to the owner’s total supported acquisition costs.

angle: Check current permit administration before converting a multi-unit building
source_label: St. Louis short-term rental permit information
local: St. Louis maintains an STR permit page with program and enforcement updates. Review current notices directly before relying on a permit assumption for an acquisition or conversion.
scope: For a small multi-unit property, map which units remain leased, become furnished rentals, or stay owner occupied. Reconcile shared improvements once and keep unit furnishing packages separate. A study engagement should state whether it covers the entire acquisition or only later additions.
records: Unit use schedule and current permit correspondence
Building acquisition reconciliation and shared-system ledger
Unit-by-unit furniture deliveries and renovation costs
scenario: A four-unit owner furnishes one vacant apartment while replacing a common entry system. The provider needs the entry system’s building-wide function and the furniture’s unit location. Treating both as costs of every listing would duplicate the same expenditure.
question: Can a planned conversion be treated as an operating STR for the estimate?
answer: Clearly label projections and unresolved approvals. The preparer should evaluate the actual or supportable operating facts before the owner relies on any tax-benefit scenario.

angle: Track ski-property renovations separately from temporary owner stays
local: Steamboat Springs publishes licensing information for STR, hosted, and temporary arrangements. Match the property’s actual license and operation to the dates in the study file.
scope: A ski-property refurbishment may span the interval between winter and summer reservations. Identify which rooms and amenities were ready at each stage, and distinguish owner stays from construction closures. Supply separate costs for unit interiors, equipment, and association projects rather than one seasonal spending total.
records: License record and booking/owner calendar
Room-by-room renovation schedule
Final interior invoices and association project notices
scenario: A condo’s bedrooms reopen while kitchen work continues, but the property is not yet offered to guests. Keep evidence of both project completion and the property’s availability. The date the first contractor finished does not alone establish the use date for everything.
question: Should off-season dates all be treated as construction downtime?
answer: No. Identify the reason for each period. Owner use, ordinary vacancy, and unavailable construction periods can require different evaluation by the return preparer.

angle: Separate resort services from the assets in an individually owned home
local: Suncadia publishes rules for rentals handled through its resort operation. Those operator rules describe that program; they are not a substitute for association documents or governmental approval for a particular property.
scope: For an individually owned resort home, distinguish guest access to resort facilities from ownership of those facilities. Obtain the management contract and identify owner-funded replacements, operating charges, and reserves. Ask the preparer to resolve membership or access payments separately from the home’s physical component costs.
records: Home deed, association documents, and resort management agreement
Reserve and replacement-purchase ledger
Owner interior inventory and separately paid access charges
scenario: A manager deducts a resort-service charge and a furniture-replacement reserve from monthly revenue. Neither line alone identifies an acquired asset. Request the contract and purchase invoices before including amounts in the property study.
question: Can resort amenities be valued as part of my home’s equipment?
answer: First establish what you own and what you merely have permission to use. The provider should analyze the supported property interest rather than allocate the resort’s facilities from advertising.

angle: Reconcile a furnished acquisition with the county property description
local: The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser offers property searches for the county. Use the parcel record to match the legal property, then separately confirm the operating requirements for its actual jurisdiction.
scope: For a purchase including furnishings, compare the deed and building description with the contract’s personal-property exhibit. Identify items installed after closing and anything the seller retained. The provider needs a reconciled acquisition total, not an added furnishing allowance that counts the same purchase consideration twice.
records: Parcel record and buyer closing statement
Executed personal-property exhibit with retained items marked
Possession-day inventory and later purchase receipts
scenario: A contract includes furnishings within the total price, while a lender’s appraisal also mentions their estimated value. Present both documents and ask the preparer to reconcile them. Adding the appraisal’s furniture figure on top of the purchase price would not explain the actual transaction.
question: Can a listing’s furnished value be used without checking the contract?
answer: No. Verify what transferred and how the agreement treats it. Estimates may inform a review, but they do not replace evidence of the acquired items and supported allocation.

angle: Keep town licensing and separate ownership interests aligned
local: Telluride publishes a town STR license resource. Confirm whether the property is in Telluride, Mountain Village, or another jurisdiction before using the town’s process for a mountain-area rental.
scope: A unit may include a separately deeded parking space, ski-storage interest, and an interior furnishing package. Supply the title and contract exhibits for each interest. Distinguish personal storage from guest amenities, and ask the preparer how each interest should enter the cost reconciliation.
records: Unit, parking, and storage title documents
Purchase agreement exhibits and furnishing inventory
Unit renovation invoices and use of retained storage
scenario: A buyer acquires a condominium and a separate parking interest under one closing statement. The study should not silently assign the parking price to bedroom furnishings or unit finishes. Identify each acquired interest before preparing component schedules.
question: Does a single closing statement mean one uniform asset?
answer: No. A transaction can include several property interests. The provider and preparer should reconcile those interests and explain the scope of the physical property analysis.

angle: Distinguish city licensing from nearby vacation-home locations
source_label: Traverse City vacation home rental licensing
local: Traverse City provides a vacation-home rental license application and renewal resource. A home marketed as a Traverse City getaway may lie outside city limits, so establish the parcel’s governing municipality first.
scope: A seasonal home may have an original cottage, later additions, and furnishings assembled over many years. Identify each addition’s construction history and distinguish purchased furnishings from transferred household items. Bring older asset schedules when the property has already been rented rather than treating a refreshed listing as a new acquisition.
records: Jurisdiction record and applicable license file
Addition plans and historical improvement invoices
Existing asset schedule and current furnishing inventory
scenario: An owner renovates a porch enclosure and introduces online bookings after years of seasonal leases. The booking platform is new, but the property history is not. Preserve the older rental and construction records when scoping the study.
question: Does changing the booking channel start a new property timeline?
answer: No. Explain the underlying acquisition and use history. The preparer needs actual changes in property and operation, not merely the date of a new online listing.

angle: Distinguish tax licensing from the casita’s physical cost schedule
source_label: Arizona Department of Revenue Tucson profile
local: Arizona’s Department of Revenue publishes Tucson licensing and local tax information. Use that resource for the applicable account questions, and separately verify land use and property-specific requirements.
scope: A casita renovation may include a small kitchen, cooling equipment, courtyard work, and utility connections shared with the main dwelling. Document which spaces each system serves. If the owner occupies the main house, identify that fact before the provider prepares a whole-parcel estimate.
records: Casita layout and main-house use description
Kitchen and cooling installation invoices
Courtyard and shared-utility scope with cost detail
scenario: A contractor installs a cooling unit in the guest casita and modifies a shared electrical service. Provide the equipment invoice and electrical scope separately. The casita’s guest-only use does not establish that the entire service upgrade serves only guests.
question: Does a city tax account determine the rental share of the property?
answer: No. The account concerns operations. Give the preparer the layout, actual use, and supported costs to evaluate the property allocation.

angle: Reconcile mandatory furnishing replacements with unit ownership
local: Vail’s Finance Department provides STR registration and application guidance. Keep the unit identifier, ownership information, and manager records aligned when requesting a study.
scope: A managed ski unit may undergo periodic replacement of beds, window treatments, or kitchen equipment. Request itemized purchases and disposal records, not just a refurbishment fee. Distinguish unit-owned items from operator-supplied equipment and association improvements before adding costs to the owner’s schedule.
records: Unit management agreement and refurbishment requirements
Itemized replacement invoices and reserve reconciliation
Removed-item log and installed-room inventory
scenario: A manager replaces mattresses under a required refurbishment program and also charges a design fee. Give the preparer the purchase and service detail rather than labeling the entire deduction from rental proceeds as furniture.
question: Can mandatory replacement charges be treated as one new asset?
answer: Ask for the underlying work and ownership detail. A fee can include goods, services, and reserves with different facts; the study should identify the actual installed components.

angle: Use the approved occupancy layout to identify the study’s rooms
local: Virginia Beach directs prospective operators to confirm eligibility and obtain necessary permits or inspections. Retain the approved layout and current address-specific operating records before relying on a rental projection.
scope: A large beach house may include sleeping rooms, owner closets, recreation areas, and multiple laundry or kitchen installations. Match the inventory to actual room functions and access. Separate additions made to increase guest capacity from existing acquired components, and identify shared building systems.
records: Approved floor plan and operating correspondence
Room-by-room furnishing and appliance inventory
Capacity-related renovation invoices and completion records
scenario: A loft is converted from storage to a furnished guest area. The project includes construction, a new bed, and electrical work. Show the prior use and final layout so the provider can distinguish the new work from the original building inventory.
question: Does a higher advertised guest capacity establish a larger deduction?
answer: No. Guest count is not a valuation method. The study needs actual acquisition costs, installed components, ownership, and use evidence.

angle: Separate the host’s operating license from an English-basement allocation
local: DC’s Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection provides housing and lodging license resources. Confirm the license appropriate to the dwelling and actual operating arrangement before preparing a study engagement.
scope: An English-basement rental may share utilities and internal stairs with an owner-occupied rowhouse. Mark private and shared areas and retain records of any conversion work. If the host is a tenant rather than the building owner, supply the lease and ownership terms for improvements and furnishings.
records: License and deed or lease for the operator’s interest
Basement plan with shared access and utility areas
Conversion invoices and guest-equipment receipts
scenario: An owner adds a kitchenette downstairs but retains an internal stairway and shared laundry for household use. Describe those connections instead of treating the suite as physically and financially independent in every respect.
question: Can a separate exterior door establish the rental allocation?
answer: No. Access is one fact. The preparer needs actual use and measurements, while the provider needs costs and system descriptions to support the property analysis.

angle: Identify the city parcel and phased completion of a new rental
local: Whitefish’s STR page describes permit and business-registration requirements within the city. Check the parcel’s jurisdiction before applying those resources to a property marketed to Whitefish visitors.
scope: For a newly completed rental, reconcile the builder’s final contract, owner-supplied equipment, and unfinished exterior work. Provide separate readiness evidence for the dwelling and later amenities. A certificate or first booking may not describe the completion of every item included in the original budget.
records: City or county confirmation and occupancy records
Builder final statement with allowances and credits
Owner purchases and separate exterior completion dates
scenario: A home opens while landscaping and a detached storage structure remain unfinished. The study file should identify completed components and clearly label outstanding work. Submitting the full contract budget without that distinction can misdescribe the property at opening.
question: Should unfinished improvements be shown as completed assets?
answer: No. Report their status and costs accurately and let the preparer evaluate the appropriate timing. Update the provider when the work and supporting invoices are complete.

angle: Check the revised zoning framework before studying a guest-cabin expansion
local: Wimberley published an August 2026 update addressing STR zoning changes and existing conditional-use permits. Review the current city guidance and your property’s approval before proceeding with expansion assumptions.
scope: A rural guest property can mix an existing home, newly built cabins, common gathering space, and land retained for personal use. Map each structure and trace costs by project. Distinguish approved plans from installed improvements, and identify infrastructure that serves several buildings.
records: Current approval and parcel site plan
Cabin construction ledgers with shared-infrastructure detail
Separate timelines for existing and new rental spaces
scenario: An owner plans two additional cabins but completes only one during the year. The infrastructure invoice serves both the completed cabin and the future site. Explain that scope and the unfinished phase rather than copying a standard per-cabin allocation.
question: Can a preserved permit establish the cost or tax treatment of new work?
answer: No. Operating approval and property-cost analysis are separate. Give the provider actual construction evidence and have the preparer evaluate ownership, timing, and use.
